jobs.title: Sr. Project Manager
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr. Project Manager based in United Kingdom.

This is an opportunity to lead complex, high-visibility projects from initial planning through successful delivery and handover. You will work across multiple workstreams, balancing strategic priorities with budgets, resources, timelines, and operational requirements. The role requires strong executive presence and the ability to engage confidently with senior stakeholders and C-level leaders. You will apply both Agile and Waterfall methodologies to adapt delivery approaches to each project’s needs. Success will depend on your ability to anticipate risks, communicate clearly, and drive accountability across teams and partners. This is a fully remote environment suited to an experienced project leader who thrives on ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Accountabilities

Define project scope, objectives, deliverables, schedules, and success criteria in partnership with executive and cross-functional stakeholders.
Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, charters, timelines, budgets, and resource allocation strategies.
Lead projects throughout the full lifecycle, from initiation and planning through execution, closure, and operational handover.
Manage project budgets, forecasts, financial performance, resource utilization, and variance analysis while identifying opportunities for cost optimization.
Coordinate internal teams, external vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain alignment and deliver project objectives.
Build strong relationships with senior leadership and C-level executives, providing clear updates, recommendations, and escalation management.
Apply Agile, Scrum, Kanban, and Waterfall methodologies according to project requirements, facilitating ceremonies and stage-gate processes as appropriate.
Track project KPIs, milestones, schedule variance, budget health, resource utilization, risks, and overall delivery performance.
Identify potential risks, dependencies, conflicts, and delivery issues, developing mitigation strategies and driving timely resolution.
Prepare executive-level presentations, dashboards, reports, and project documentation covering progress, risks, decisions, and key performance indicators.
Lead process improvement initiatives, capture lessons learned, and establish best practices to improve future project delivery.
Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards and coordinate formal handover, documentation, archiving, and closure of outstanding contractual or financial activities.

Requirements

5+ years of proven project management experience, with responsibility for leading projects from conception through completion.
Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, forecasting, financial analysis, resource allocation, and cost control.
Advanced knowledge of Agile and Waterfall project management methodologies, including Scrum and Kanban.
Experience working directly with senior stakeholders, executives, and C-level leadership.
Proficiency with project management and tracking tools such as Jira, Trello, MS Project, or equivalent platforms.
Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly PowerPoint for executive presentations and Excel for financial and project analysis.
Strong ability to define, monitor, analyze, and communicate project KPIs and performance metrics.
Excellent written and spoken English, with strong presentation, negotiation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field preferred; a Master's degree is a plus.
PMP, PMI-ACP, or another relevant project management certification is strongly preferred.
Strategic mindset with the ability to connect project objectives to broader organizational goals.
Strong problem-solving, risk management, organizational, and decision-making skills.
Ability to balance strategic priorities with close attention to operational details.
Adaptability and confidence working in dynamic environments with shifting priorities.
Collaborative leadership style with the ability to build cohesive teams and maintain strong working relationships.

Benefits

Fully remote work arrangement.
Opportunity to lead high-visibility and strategically important projects.
Exposure to senior leadership and complex cross-functional initiatives.
Professional growth through continuous learning, training, and mentorship.
Supportive and collaborative remote team environment.

At Medius, we believe managing finance should be about strategy, not stress. That same mindset shapes not only the solutions we build, but also the culture we create for our people. We remove complexity, embrace innovation, and give our teams the freedom to focus on what truly matters — whether that’s transforming the future of finance with AI or finding balance to go home on time.

Founded in Sweden in 2001, Medius has grown from a local startup into a global leader in cloud-based spend management solutions. Our journey has been driven by continuous innovation, a passion for technology, and above all — the people who make it happen.

We’re more than a software company. We’re a team of problem-solvers, innovators and collaborators working together to reinvent the category of accounts payable. Our solutions use Artificial Intelligence to eliminate manual work, bring clarity, confidence, and control, and empower finance teams of the future.

jobs.description:
Company Overview

ImmunityBio is a vertically integrated commercial stage biotechnology company developing next-generation therapies that bolster the natural immune system to defeat cancers and infectious diseases. The Company’s range of immunotherapy and cell therapy platforms, alone and together, act to drive and sustain an immune response with the goal of creating durable and safe protection against disease. Designated an FDA Breakthrough Therapy, ANKTIVA is the first FDA-approved immunotherapy for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer CIS that activates NK cells, T cells, and memory T cells for a long-duration response. The Company is applying its science and platforms to treating cancers, including the development of potential cancer vaccines, as well as developing immunotherapies and cell therapies that we believe sharply reduce or eliminate the need for standard high-dose chemotherapy. These platforms and their associated product candidates are designed to be more effective, accessible, and easily administered than current standards of care in oncology and infectious diseases.

Why ImmunityBio?

ImmunityBio is developing cutting-edge technology with the goal to transform the lives of patients with cancer and develop next-generation therapies and vaccines that complement, harness and amplify the immune system to defeat cancers and infectious diseases.
Opportunity to join a publicly traded biopharmaceutical company with headquarters in Southern California.

Ability to join a growing company with professional development opportunities.

Position Summary

The Principal Program Manager, Engineering Projects leads a portfolio of complex capital, facility, utility, equipment, and technical-infrastructure programs that enable ImmunityBio’s clinical and commercial GMP manufacturing operations. This role provides strategic program leadership from concept development and capital approval through design, construction, commissioning, qualification, operational handover, and closeout. The Principal Program Manager establishes integrated governance, portfolio priorities, execution strategy, project controls, and executive decision support; leads cross-functional internal teams and external engineering, construction, CQV, and vendor partners; and ensures programs are delivered safely, compliantly, on schedule, within approved capital budgets, and in alignment with business, quality, and regulatory requirements.

Direct capital planning and financial controls, including business cases, appropriation requests, budget baselines, forecasting, cash-flow management, invoice review, vendor performance, and change-order governance.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science or relevant field required.
10+ years of progressively responsible experience leading engineering, facilities, manufacturing, validation, or capital-project programs, including at least 6 years managing complex projects in a GMP-regulated biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, medical-device, or similarly regulated manufacturing environment is required.
Experience delivering capital projects through design, construction, commissioning, qualification, operational handover, and closeout, including ownership of scope, schedule, budget, risk, contractor coordination, and change control is required.
Experience with facility buildouts and equipment CQV strongly preferred.
Experience leading capital or infrastructure projects involving construction, utilities, and equipment installation in cGMP or similarly regulated environments preferred.
Experience working with cross-functional teams, external design and construction partners, and multiple stakeholders in a matrixed organization preferred.
PMP or other project management certification preferred.

Demonstrated knowledge and application of stage-gate, predictive, and hybrid project-delivery methodologies appropriate to regulated capital, engineering, and CQV environments.

Strong experience facilitating project team meetings, cross-functional communication and decision making, and ensuring alignment with internal and external stakeholders.

Demonstrated ability to think strategically when planning, managing teams, and managing processes.

Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail and compliance.

KWI keeps specialty retail running for Pandora, Bluemercury, Tom Ford, and dozens of other brands, and behind every storefront is an engineering team shipping constantly. Job Title:
Technical Project Manager

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

You will be our first dedicated project manager, and your job is to fix that. You own the work breakdown structure and the integrated schedule. You run the weekly coordination rhythm, record every task and decision so nothing is dropped, and stay ahead of the risks that quietly kill hardware schedules: long-lead parts, manpower shortages and skill gaps, missing equipment and infrastructure. Leadership will continue to set priorities, assign responsibility, and hold people accountable; your job is to make the plan legible and current so those decisions are made with real information, and so every person on the team knows what they need to be doing and when.

This is a role for someone who treats a well-built Gantt chart as a love language. Your best days end with the ambiguity banished from the plan and a name and a date on everything that matters. We are a startup: the process you bring must be the lightweight 20% that delivers 80% of the value, not a bureaucracy the team routes around.

Essential Duties

Schedule & WBS Ownership (Primary)

Build and own the work breakdown structure across our product lines: decompose engineering, manufacturing, test, and delivery work into tasks with owners, durations, dependencies, and dates
Build and maintain the integrated master schedule in a Gantt-based tool; keep it current enough that the team and leadership trust it as the single source of truth for what happens when
Identify and track the critical path; flag slips early and quantify their downstream impact so leadership can re-prioritize before a deadline is blown, not after
Translate customer commitments, demo dates, and test events into backward-planned schedules with explicit margin

Risk & Dependency Management

Maintain a living risk register for the things that actually derail hardware programs: long-lead and allocated parts, manpower shortages and skill gaps, missing equipment, tooling, and facility/infrastructure needs
Chase dependencies across engineering, purchasing, and the shop: surface the part that isn’t ordered, the fixture that isn’t built, and the test range that isn’t booked while there is still time to fix it
Work with the buyer on long-lead procurement timing so build schedules are planned around real lead times, and with leadership on staffing gaps before they become schedule slips

Coordination, Tasking & Communication

Run the weekly coordination meeting: set the agenda, drive it to decisions, and finish with every action item recorded with an owner and a due date
Be the recorder of tasking for the company: capture tasks and decisions from meetings, hallway conversations, and test events into one tracked system so nothing is missed or forgotten
Follow up on open actions between meetings; keep status honest without becoming the person the team hides from
Give leadership a clear, current picture of status, risks, and upcoming decisions that is short, factual, and free of surprises

Building the Structure

Stand up the company’s project management practices from scratch: task tracking, schedule reviews, action-item discipline, and deliverable definitions where none formally exist today
Select and administer the scheduling and task-tracking tools the company will run on, sized for a lean team: powerful enough to be trusted, light enough to be used
Establish just enough process to bring order to tasking and project planning without slowing a fast-iterating R&D team

Requirements

5+ years of project management experience on complex hardware / electromechanical development programs in robotics, defense, aerospace, automotive, industrial equipment, or similar
Technical background: an engineering degree or hands-on engineering experience on hardware products. You must be able to follow a technical discussion, ask credible questions, and earn the respect of a senior engineering team
Demonstrated ownership of a WBS and integrated schedule on a multi-disciplinary program: you built and ran the plan, not just reported on it
Expert fluency in Gantt-based scheduling tools (Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or similar): critical path, dependencies, baselines, and resource loading
Proven risk management on hardware programs, with a track record of catching long-lead, staffing, and equipment problems before they hit the schedule
Strong meeting facilitation and action-tracking discipline: you run tight meetings that end in owners and dates, and you close loops relentlessly
Comfortable leading through influence rather than authority: in this role, leadership sets priorities and holds people accountable; you make the plan visible, current, and impossible to ignore
Self-sufficient in a low-process environment: you impose structure on ambiguity rather than waiting for structure to be handed to you
US person (citizen or lawful permanent resident), required for ITAR compliance

Nice-to-Have

PMP, PMI-SP, or similar project management certification
Experience in a defense, ITAR-regulated, or government-customer environment, including milestone reviews, test events, and customer-driven schedules
Experience taking a hardware product from prototype through production transfer
Experience standing up project management practices at a startup or small company, rather than operating inside an established PMO
Working familiarity with manufacturing and machine-shop workflows, enough to plan realistically around fabrication, assembly, and test

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, a real WBS and integrated schedule exist and the team trusts them. The weekly coordination meeting runs on rails, every task has an owner and a date in one tracked system, and the first schedule-threatening risks (a long-lead part, a skills gap, a missing piece of equipment) have been caught and raised while they were still cheap to fix.
On an ongoing basis, nothing falls through the cracks. Everyone on the team can tell you what they need to be doing and when it is due. Leadership sets priorities against a schedule that reflects reality, slips are seen weeks out instead of discovered at the deadline, and the company hits its demo and delivery commitments because the plan was honest all along.

Work Environment

This role is based on-site in Austin, TX at our shop, working directly alongside the engineering and manufacturing team; the plan gets built by walking the floor, not from a remote dashboard. The environment is a working R&D and manufacturing facility for weapons systems: expect an active shop floor and proximity to live-fire test activity, with strict adherence to safety protocols. Occasional travel to test ranges and demonstration events to keep the schedule connected to what actually happens in the field.

Benefits

Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.
Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.
Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.
The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.
100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.
Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.
Zero Red Tape: You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.
Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.
Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

About The Interview

Initial screen with recruiter (30 min phone call)
Virtual interview with Director of HW Ops (45 min via MS Teams)
In-person interview (1 hour in Austin, TX) *9 Mothers will fly out candidates that are not local to the Austin area
Reference checks & offer

Compensation Range: $125K - $150K

jobs.description:
Salary Range: $100,999 - $134,665

Relocation Offered: No

About Us

Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC, headquartered in Dallas, is a regulated electricity transmission and distribution business that uses superior asset management skills to provide reliable electricity delivery to consumers. Oncor (together with its subsidiaries) operates the largest transmission and distribution system in Texas, delivering power to nearly 4 million homes and businesses and operating more than 145,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in Texas.

Summary

The Regional Security Manager is responsible for executing Oncor’s Corporate Security (physical) program across a defined geographic region. This role ensures the protection of critical infrastructure, substations, field assets, and personnel through the application of enterprise security standards, risk-based controls, and operational discipline.

This position requires an autonomous professional who can translate enterprise security strategy into field execution in a geographically dispersed, high-risk critical infrastructure environment. The successful candidate will be required to be based out of West Texas and when not conducting field work, the primary reporting location for this position will be our office in Odessa.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Execute enterprise physical security strategy across the assigned region, ensuring alignment with corporate standards and risk tolerance for critical grid infrastructure.
Lead or co-lead regional physical security operations including:
Risk Assessments
Investigations
Incident Response
Site Surveys
Vendor Relationships
Law Enforcement Liaison
Conduct risk and vulnerability assessments across T&D infrastructure
Develop and implement layered security controls appropriate for utility environments, including remote and unmanned sites
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory and industry frameworks, including:
NERC CIP physical security requirements
Internal corporate security policies and standards
Lead regional incident response for physical security events, including:
Intrusions, vandalism, and theft
Sabotage or targeted attacks
Coordination with Enterprise Security & Resilience Center (ESRC)
Incident reporting and corrective actions

Monitor and assess regional threat environment and adjust posture accordingly
Oversee security technology deployment and operations, including:
Access control systems (ACS)
Video surveillance (CCTV, analytics)
Intrusion detection systems

Partner with engineering, operations, and capital projects teams to ensure security-by-design for:
New substations and infrastructure builds
Grid modernization projects
Hardening of existing assets
Manage and optimize third-party security vendors, including guard services, system integrators, and maintenance providers
Define and enforce SLAs and performance KPIs

Develop and maintain regional procedures, response protocols, and site-specific security plans
Build and maintain relationships with:
Local, state, and federal law enforcement
Fusion centers and intelligence-sharing groups

Lead regional security awareness efforts targeting field personnel, operators, and contractors
Develop, monitor, and report on regional metrics, including:
Security incidents at substations and facilities
Response times and law enforcement coordination
Technology health and effectiveness
Vendor performance

Provide regional input into executive-level reporting, including risk trends, mitigation progress, and emerging threats
Act as a change agent to elevate physical security maturity in a traditionally operational field environment
Build strong cross-functional partnerships
Perform all essential functions and other duties as assigned
Travel within Texas is required, approximately 50–60%, including frequent visits to remote field locations

Education & Experience

High school diploma, GED, or equivalent is required
Bachelor’s degree is encouraged to apply
7+ years in physical security, law enforcement, military, or critical infrastructure protection is required
5+ years managing multi-site or regional security operations is encouraged to apply
Experience responding to or managing incidents impacting operational resilience
Strong vendor management experience across guard force and electronic security systems providers

Skills

Deep understanding of physical security application in critical infrastructure environments
Ability to assess and prioritize risk across large geographic territories
Strong operational leadership in dynamic, field-based environments
Effective coordination with operations during high-impact events (storms, outages, attacks)
Strong communication and stakeholder influence skills across technical and non-technical groups
Analytical mindset with ability to translate incident data into actionable improvements
Experience with physical security systems in harsh or remote environments
Crisis leadership and decision-making under pressure
Strong organizational and execution discipline

Measures of Success

Effective implementation of layered security controls at critical sites
High performance and reliability of security technologies in field environments
Strong coordination with operations during incidents and storm response
Establish and maintain strong relationships with Law Enforcement partners
Demonstrated improvement in overall physical security maturity across the region

Physical Requirements

This role includes both office-based work and frequent field activity across a geographically dispersed region. The individual must be able to perform the essential job functions listed below:

Travel extensively (approximately 50–60%) within the assigned region, including driving long distances and accessing remote or rural locations. Focus of this will mainly be West TX
Conduct site visits and inspections at substations, field facilities, and other operational environments
Walk and stand for extended periods and navigate uneven terrain, including gravel, dirt, and undeveloped surfaces
Work outdoors in varying environmental conditions, which may include extreme heat, cold, wind, or precipitation
Lift, carry, push, and/or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds
Perform physical movements such as bending, stooping, kneeling, reaching, and climbing as necessary to complete site assessments and inspections

Maintain situational awareness and the ability to safely operate in active industrial and field environments.

The Physical Security Manager
is responsible for the operational management and execution of the credit union's physical security program. Reporting to the Director of Security, this position oversees daily security operations, Security Operations Center activities, security systems, and assigned personnel to help ensure the safety and security of associates, members, facilities, cash assets, and the organization's reputation.

The Physical Security Manager implements security strategies, policies, and procedures established by the Director of Security and serves as the primary operational leader for physical security activities across the organization. This position partners closely with departments including Fraud, Risk, Information Security, Human Resources, Facilities, and Operations to identify vulnerabilities, mitigate risks, and ensure effective security practices throughout the credit union.

Security Strategy, Governance & Program Leadership

Implement physical security policies, standards, procedures, and initiatives established by the Director of Security.
Manage day-to-day security operations and supervise assigned security personnel and Security Operations Center activities.
Monitor security program effectiveness and recommend operational improvements.
Support organization-wide security awareness and compliance efforts.
Provide operational guidance to managers and associates on physical security matters.
Act on behalf of the Director of Security when designated and provide leadership during their absence.

Physical Security Operations & Systems

Manage the daily operation of the Security Operations Center, including monitoring activities, incident response, and personnel coordination.
Oversee administration of access control systems, surveillance platforms, alarm systems, visitor management tools, and related technologies.
Coordinate equipment maintenance, testing, repairs, upgrades, and vendor support activities.
Monitor security operations across branch, ATM, and administrative locations to ensure compliance with established standards.
Conduct facility reviews and recommend security enhancements as needed.
Support implementation of physical security requirements for new facilities, remodels, relocations, and ATM deployments.

Risk Management, Assessments & Compliance

Conduct security assessments, inspections, and vulnerability reviews across credit union facilities.
Identify risks involving robbery, burglary, workplace violence, unauthorized access, fraud, and other security concerns.
Recommend corrective actions and assist with implementation of approved mitigation plans.
Support internal audits, examinations, and regulatory reviews related to physical security.
Maintain documentation supporting assessments, incidents, investigations, and compliance activities.
Partner with internal departments to address operational security concerns and emerging threats.

Incident Response & Investigations

Respond to and coordinate security incidents, threats, emergencies, and investigative activities.
Manage robbery response procedures, duress protocols, workplace violence response, and employee safety initiatives.
Coordinate with law enforcement agencies, emergency responders, and internal stakeholders during incidents.
Conduct investigations and gather evidence, documentation, video recordings, and other relevant information.
Perform post-incident reviews and implement approved corrective actions.
Escalate significant incidents and emerging threats to the Director of Security and other leadership as appropriate.

Security Awareness & Organizational Readiness

Deliver security training and awareness programs for associates and management.
Reinforce compliance with security policies, procedures, and operational standards.
Provide guidance regarding robbery response, suspicious activity, workplace violence prevention, and emergency procedures.
Support organizational preparedness through exercises, drills, and response planning activities.
Assist with development and maintenance of security procedures, reference materials, and training resources.

Vendor, Law Enforcement & Stakeholder Relationships

Maintain day-to-day working relationships with law enforcement agencies, monitoring providers, and security vendors.
Coordinate vendor service activities, maintenance schedules, and support requests.
Monitor vendor performance and communicate service concerns and improvement opportunities.
Collaborate with Fraud, Risk, Information Security, Human Resources, Facilities, and Operations teams to address security issues.
Maintain effective communication with associates and management regarding security-related activities and concerns.

Reporting, Analytics & Continuous Improvement

Prepare reports regarding incidents, investigations, assessments, inspections, and Security Operations Center activity.
Monitor trends and identify opportunities to improve security controls, processes, and operational effectiveness.

Assist with implementation of security initiatives, technology enhancements, and continuous improvement efforts.

Prior supervisory or management experience preferred.
Experience conducting investigations, incident response, and security assessments.
Experience with access control, video surveillance, alarm systems, and security-related technologies.
Financial institution, banking, credit union, or other regulated industry experience preferred.

Leading programs at Uber means setting direction in motion, not waiting for perfect conditions. Stakeholder management skills, including in delivering change management projects to launch new enterprise-wide tools or systems;

jobs.description:
事業概要

すべての経済活動のデジタル化を目指す株式会社LayerXは、Ai Workforce事業部において、「AIを業務に溶け込ませる」をコンセプトとした生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。
Ai Workforce事業部は2023年に発足した新規事業チームであり、幅広い業界のエンタープライズ企業パートナーとの取り組みを積み重ねてきました。大規模言語モデル（LLM）などのAIの技術は飛躍的に発展していますが、それ単体では本格的な業務で使うことが難しく、そのギャップを埋めるUX (AI-UX) を実現することを目指しています。
実証実験（PoC）ではなく、プロダクトとして既に続々とお客様にご導入いただいており、AIのポテンシャルを活かす更なるプロダクトの進化や、市場の拡大に取り組んでいます。

募集背景

Ai Workforce事業部では、日本を代表する大手企業を対象に、生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。

金融業界は、「膨大な非構造データ」と「厳密なルール」に基づく情報産業であり、膨大な書類の確認・審査等の人間がテキストを読んで判断・作成する業務が多く、LLM導入により劇的なコスト削減や収益向上が見込める領域です。

jobs.title: Functional Consultant/ Project Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

At Medius, we believe managing finance should be about strategy, not stress. That same mindset shapes not only the solutions we build, but also the culture we create for our people. We remove complexity, embrace innovation, and give our teams the freedom to focus on what truly matters — whether that’s transforming the future of finance with AI or finding balance to go home on time.

Founded in Sweden in 2001, Medius has grown from a local startup into a global leader in cloud-based spend management solutions. Today, thousands of organizations worldwide trust us to simplify accounts payable and spend management processes. Our journey has been driven by continuous innovation, a passion for technology, and above all — the people who make it happen.

We’re more than a software company. We’re a team of problem-solvers, innovators and collaborators working together to reinvent the category of accounts payable. Our solutions use Artificial Intelligence to eliminate manual work, bring clarity, confidence, and control, and empower finance teams of the future.

At Medius,
our values guide how we work and grow together:

Connect – We believe in the power of people—individually and collectively—and our success depends on understanding and respecting each other. We appreciate that ‘empowering finance teams of the future’ is an exciting endeavor, and we share it with everyone around us.
Question – We enjoy the challenge of our work and the thrill of collaboration. We are not afraid to question ourselves and each other because we believe diverse perspectives can lead to better outcomes and that there is great power in resolution.
Own – We are thorough, thoughtful, and decisive. We anticipate what’s next, what a customer might need, and then we deliver. That’s how we get things done. And that’s how we remain a leader. Customers trust us to do our job so that they can focus on what they do best.

At Medius, you’ll join a diverse, global community where curiosity is celebrated, ideas matter, and innovation never stops. If you’re passionate about technology, eager to make an impact, and ready to grow alongside a team that lives its values, Medius is where you can do your best work — your impact is global.

Learn more at www.medius.com

Job Overview

As a Project Manager / Functional Consultant
, you will join the Medius Professional Services team and lead projects implementing our spend management suite for customers. From day one, you will take on significant responsibility, managing complex and engaging projects across both local and international markets.

You will guide customers through the full onboarding lifecycle, including solution design, deployment, UAT, go-live, and hypercare. This is a hybrid role combining project management and functional consulting responsibilities. Depending on project scope and complexity, you may focus on one area or balance both, with opportunities over time to specialize based on your strengths and interests.

Responsibilities And Duties

Lead end-to-end project delivery, including planning, resourcing, milestone tracking, and budget management
Facilitate workshops and deliver training sessions (on-site or remote)
Configure Medius solutions based on customer requirements and best practices
Support customers throughout testing phases, go-live, and hypercare
Analyze customers’ existing spend management processes and identify improvement opportunities
Drive process optimization initiatives in collaboration with customers
Produce and maintain solution documentation, including specifications and change requests
Provide regular reporting and updates to project stakeholders

Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of experience in IT system implementations, ideally in cloud-based/SaaS environments as a Functional Consultant
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a proactive and solution-oriented mindset
Business-oriented and results-driven approach
Ability to manage multiple parallel tasks while maintaining quality and control
Solid understanding of IT systems and implementation methodologies
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken

Preferred:

Experience in Spend Management solutions
Previous experience in a consulting role
Familiarity with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics AX / Finance & Operations, Dynamics NAV / Business Central, SAP, or Infor M3
Medius is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant skills, experience, qualifications, certifications, internal equity, and the geographic location in which the role is performed. Compensation may vary for roles performed in different locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total compensation package for this position may also include eligibility for variable compensation (such as a performance bonus or commission), benefits, and/or participation in other incentive or benefit plans, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans. Benefits may include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, and retirement benefits, subject to eligibility requirements.

Medius is an equal opportunity employer
. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees, without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity or expression), national origin, ancestry, age, disability (physical or mental), genetic information, medical condition, marital status, citizenship or immigration status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

If you require a reasonable accommodation due to a disability or for religious reasons during the application or interview process, please review our accommodations process.

You’ll surface fraud trends, size risk, and help shape the strategy that protects our players and our platform, while keeping the experience frictionless for the vast majority of legitimate users. You're a great fit if you're comfortable digging into messy, high-volume transactional data, enjoy translating findings into clear recommendations, and want your analysis to directly influence how PrizePicks fights fraud.

What You'll Do:

Deliver analytical work that actually moves the needle — protecting the platform while making the experience better for good players.
Build, document, and maintain easy-to-use, insightful dashboards and reusable analyses that monitor fraud performance and key risk indicators.
Distill complex datasets into recommendations with clear visualizations and concise talking points for non-technical stakeholders.
Partner with Engineering, Fraud Ops and Product to identify and close data, performance, and process gaps.
Conduct deep-dive analyses to support fraud-related business decisions with data-driven insights and recommendations.
Scope and complete ad-hoc data requests around fraud trends and product initiatives.

What You'll Have:

Experience

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Statistics, Finance, Mathematics, Analytics, or a related field
2+ years of experience in risk analytics, fraud detection, or a related data-focused field, preferably within online gaming, Daily Fantasy Sports, or fintech
Working understanding of common fraud vectors in an online transactional environment (payment fraud, identity fraud, bonus abuse, etc.) and how fraud controls can impact legitimate user experience

Technical Skills

Advanced SQL for extracting, manipulating, and analyzing data
Data visualization experience (e.g., Tableau)
Strong Excel skills
Python experience a plus (automation, modeling, or statistical analysis)

Soft Skills

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts to non-technical audiences
Detail-oriented with a high standard for accuracy in data analysis and reporting
Judgment to balance fraud risk against player experience — knows that over-blocking good players is its own kind of cost
Organized, reliable, curious, and growth-oriented team player
Demonstrated ability with data-driven critical thinking, problem-solving, and recommendations

Where you’ll live:

While we prefer candidates based in Atlanta, we are open to qualified applicants from anywhere in the U.S. and are willing to consider remote candidates.

Working at PrizePicks:

The typical salary range for this position is $100,000 to $110,000. At PrizePicks, we consider your role, level, and where you'll be working when determining our salary ranges. The compensation info you see on our job postings gives you an idea of the starting pay range for the position. Your actual pay within that range will depend on your specific work location, as well as your skills, experience, and education. Your recruiter will be happy to chat more about the specific pay range for your location and how we arrived at it during the hiring process.

This application period will remain open for 30 days. We’re committed to finding the best candidate, so this date may be adjusted, and any changes will be reflected in this posting.

Date Posted: 8/25/26

Benefits you’ll receive:

In addition to your great compensation package, full-time employees will be eligible for the following perks:

Company-subsidized medical, dental, & vision plans
401(k) plan with company match
Annual bonus
Flexible PTO to encourage a healthy work/life balance (2 weeks STRONGLY encouraged!)
Generous paid leave programs, including 16-week paid parental leave and disability benefits
Workplace flexibility and modern work schedules focused on getting the job done, not hours clocked
Company-wide in-person events and team outings
Lifestyle enhancement program
Company equipment provided (Windows & Mac options)
Annual performance reviews with opportunities for growth and career development

You must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

Description

RMC is seeking a highly motivated
Program Analyst
to support our customers at the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia.

Are you ready to embark on a fulfilling and impactful career journey with RMC Global? We're in search of an exceptional Program Analyst
to become a part of our mission-driven team, dedicated to making a difference in the federal and commercial markets. At RMC, we're all about enhancing security for both our military and global commercial partners, offering an array of services such as Risk Management, Mission Assurance, and Cybersecurity.

Our team's well-being is paramount, and we reflect this commitment through our flexible work environment and exceptional company culture. By joining RMC, you become a key contributor to our mission – Assuring Tomorrow!

When you join RMC, you'll experience a range of benefits, including:

Comprehensive health, vision, and dental insurance plans fully covered for employees
Subsidized dependent health care coverage

Participation in our Annual Bonus Program
Life insurance policy equivalent to 1x your annual salary.
Company paid short and long-term disability
Cell phone reimbursement of $65 per month
401(k) Plan with contributions
A 401(k) Safe Harbor Employer Contribution Program, which includes a 3% contribution

Position Summary

The Program Analyst (PA) supports RMC’s military customers and program personnel, including the Mission Assurance Assessment and Utility Assessment teams worldwide. In this role, the PA provides technical and operational coordination, training, and support to a military headquarters entity, assisting Joint Service as needed. Responsibilities include planning, organizing, and preparing information briefs and point papers on policies, procedures, and operations, as well as reviewing military headquarters plans for compliance with DoD directives. Additionally, the PA offers administrative support to RMC Corporate Headquarters and gains expertise in various specialty areas, including Law Enforcement, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and High-Yield Explosive protection, Antiterrorism, Physical Security, Information Sharing, Emergency Management, Supporting Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and Communications.

Essential Functions

Planning, Coordinating, and Executing Assessments:

Support military customer in the coordination, preparation, research and execution of assessments, events, activities to support Joint Staff, Navy, and Marine Corps Mission Assurance and its related programs and processes
Assist with event planning, meetings, and conferences, including maintaining a master event calendar or spreadsheet, collecting RSVPs, and coordinating with external stakeholders
Provide logistical and administrative support to RMC personnel for domestic and international travel as needed
Schedule meetings with military installations

DOD Product Development And Mission Assurance Support

Support military customer in the preparation and review of graphical, oral, written reports, briefs, and products for multiple programs encompassed within the Mission Assurance umbrella
Assist in the development and review of DoD reports and information papers, white papers, and position papers
Assist in the coordination of staffing and research for DoD initiatives
Draft briefs for internal and external use on various protection related topics
Edit, proofread, and fact-check various documents and reports
Participate in conferences, meetings, and other events, as needed
Sit-in on working groups to develop program awareness and subject matter expertise

Process RMC mail, maintaining and disseminating confidential information to the appropriate parties
Work with PA Team to maintain a stock of shirts on hand for assessments and company events
Assist RMC personnel with office access when needed
Assist with support and administrative tasks for end of year company meeting
Assist in various administrative duties, as needed

RMC Functional and Business Area Support

Support RMC functional and business areas when needed (PMO, Energy Resilience, AHTA, Cyber, etc.)
Maintain and work with RMC and government personnel to meet contractual requirements
Research, evaluate solutions, make recommendations, and present on various topics to RMC and government/military personnel
Assist in drafting, editing, proofreading, and guiding policy through a review process

Security Coordination

Assist RMC personnel in Common Access Card (CAC) processing
Assist RMC personnel gain access to NIPR and SIPR accounts
Serve as a member of the Security Coordination Team
Escorting RMC personnel onsite at Pentagon
Access Defense Information Security System (DISS) and coordinate DISS data and/or security clearances as necessary for job requirements. Ensure the information in DISS is secured at the highest level. Keep DISS information confidential per the RMC Employee Non-Disclosure Agreement

Competencies

Exhibits strong organizational skills and attention to detail, effectively prioritizing tasks and managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment
Develops clear and concise plans for completing projects and achieving objectives, utilizing superb research, analytical, writing, and editing skills
Ability to draft and send professionally polished emails that convey key actions, needs, and recommendations
Customer service-oriented and experienced in providing support to client personnel while working collaboratively and constructively with team members
Able to identify issues for management, perform needs-gap analysis, collect data to support conclusions
Strong work ethic and independence; effectively applies technical knowledge to solve problems
Can identify, test, and utilize new tools to enhance organization, communication, and products
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and Software (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, etc)

Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree
Minimum 1 year of work experience to include work-study, internships, or a combination thereof
Military service is a plus but not a requirement

Security Clearance: Obtaining a DoD Secret Clearance. Applicants selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for clearance level required for the job.
Valid Passport: Possession of a current passport with a minimum of 8 months remaining until the expiration date.

Ability to maintain and access NIPR/SIPR accounts by monthly travel to employees designated regional site.
Travel Flexibility: Willingness and capability to travel, Choose an item. approximately 25-35% of the time.
Telecommunication is authorized for this role.

Environmental, Health, Safety & Security Manager
jobs.description:
About Giga

Giga is building gigawatts of AI data centers to hasten a future of intelligence and abundance. We build data centers fast and at scale by combining the capabilities of an equipment supplier, engineering firm, general contractor, and real estate developer under one roof. Our team moves quickly and thinks practically. If you're ready to make an impact in an industry that matters, we're looking for people like you.

Why join Giga

The Pace: We're building at a speed most companies talk about but never actually operate at. If you've been bored somewhere else, you won't be here.
The Impact: Every person at Giga touches the work that matters. No layers, no waiting for approval chains. You'll see your fingerprints on what we ship.
The Team: A team of operators defining the future of AI infrastructure. We recruit A-players from the most innovative companies in the world, and they choose Giga because the work here means more.
The Moment: AI doesn't run without power, and that's us. Giga is the picks and shovels behind the AI revolution. This industry is about to explode, and you'll be in the room where it's already happening.

What You’ll Do

As the EHS & S Manager,
you will own the full Environmental, Health, Safety & Security (EHS&S) function at our Houston manufacturing facility — from OSHA and environmental regulatory compliance to hazard-specific programs covering high-voltage electrical testing, transformer oil/dielectric fluid handling, overhead crane operations, and hot work. You'll also serve as the site lead for physical security, access control, and emergency preparedness. You'll work closely with plant leadership, production supervisors, and corporate HSE to build a proactive safety culture and keep the facility fully compliant with federal, state, and local requirements.

Where you’ll work

We are an in-office culture — velocity matters when you're building physical infrastructure, and the best decisions happen in the room. This role is based full-time on-site at our Houston, TX manufacturing facility, with regular presence on the production floor, testing areas, and warehouse/yard.

Responsibilities

Environmental, Health & Safety Program Leadership

Develop, implement, and maintain the facility's written HSE programs in compliance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910 (General Industry) and applicable EPA/TCEQ environmental regulations
Own facility-specific safety programs including electrical safety/arc flash (NFPA 70E) for 480V system testing, lockout/tagout, overhead crane and rigging safety, hot work, and PPE
Manage safe handling, storage, and spill response procedures for mineral oil-based transformer dielectric fluid and other regulated fluids used in production and testing
Lead job hazard analyses (JHAs) for manufacturing, testing, and maintenance operations, and ensure controls are implemented and followed
Conduct regular facility safety inspections and audits; track findings to closure and drive continuous improvement in safety performance
Investigate incidents, near-misses, and injuries; determine root cause and implement corrective/preventive actions
Maintain OSHA recordkeeping (300/300A/301 logs) and ensure timely, accurate incident reporting to OSHA and internal stakeholders
Manage the facility's industrial hygiene program, including noise, air quality, and exposure monitoring where applicable

Environmental Compliance

Maintain compliance with applicable air, water, waste, and chemical storage regulations (e.g., SPCC, hazardous waste generator requirements, stormwater permits)
Manage environmental permits, inspections, and regulatory reporting for the Houston facility
Oversee proper handling, storage, and disposal of used transformer oil, solvents, and other regulated waste streams

Training & Culture

Develop and deliver HSE training, including HAZCOM, electrical safety, LOTO, crane/rigging, confined space (as applicable), PPE, and emergency response
Partner with plant leadership and supervisors to build a strong site-wide safety culture and hold teams accountable to HSE standards
Maintain training records and certifications for all employees and relevant contractors

Security

Manage physical security for the facility, including access control systems, badge/visitor management, and security camera systems
Develop and maintain site security procedures, including protocols for after-hours access, contractor/vendor access, and asset protection
Serve as the facility's primary point of contact for security incidents, and coordinate with local law enforcement as needed
Conduct periodic security risk assessments and recommend improvements to physical security controls

Emergency Preparedness

Develop and maintain the facility's Emergency Action Plan, including evacuation procedures, severe weather (hurricane) response, and medical emergency response
Coordinate emergency drills and ensure employees are trained on emergency procedures
Maintain relationships with local fire, EMS, and emergency management agencies

Reporting & Leadership

Report on EHS&S performance metrics, incident trends, and program status to plant and corporate leadership
Manage the EHS&S budget for the facility, including PPE, training, equipment, and contracted services
Serve as the facility's primary point of contact for OSHA, environmental agencies, and other regulatory bodies during inspections or audits

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of progressive EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment, including at least 2 years in a leadership/managerial role
Strong working knowledge of OSHA 1910 General Industry standards, including electrical safety, LOTO, and crane/material handling requirements
Experience managing environmental compliance programs in a manufacturing setting

Job Description

The Environmental Business Line of AECOM is seeking a Hazardous Building Material/Industrial Hygiene Project Manager for immediate employment with the Northeast department of the EHS & Air Practice. This candidate is expected to report to the Boston, MA, Chelmsford, MA, or Manchester, NH office.

The appropriately qualified applicant will be able to demonstrate at least 8 years of experience performing and managing building hazardous material (asbestos, lead paint, etc.) surveys, abatement oversight, and design and/or industrial hygiene projects. This is anticipated to be a seller/doer role, combining technical project execution with business development. On the business development side, responsibilities will include identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, developing client relationships, and securing contracts (both internally and externally). This dual role requires a balance of technical expertise, project management skills, and business acumen to successfully grow the business while delivering exceptional service to clients.

The job responsibilities for this position will include but are not limited to:
Managing and/or self-performing a wide range of hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects for both private and public-sector clients
Collaborating with other licensed/certified professionals and technical/regulatory specialists on hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects. These projects are expected to include survey and investigation work, abatement/remediation design, and abatement/remediation.
Provide technical and/or regulatory leadership for hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects throughout New England, the US, and internationally.
Develop proposals, including work scope, budgets and schedules for hazardous building material survey/design/abatement and other industrial hygiene projects.
Manage or provide review of technical work and field activities, including performing oversight of projects to confirm work is being done in accordance with the contracted scope of work, budget, schedule and regulatory/industry standards.
Review, coordinate or prepare written reports, work plans, and technical memorandum; analyze data and develop supported conclusions.
Work collaboratively with other teams within the EHS department, Environment business line, and across AECOM’s other internal business lines.
Proactively identify opportunities to increase project efficiencies and add value to client service offerings.
Identifying and pursuing new business opportunities and supporting department growth through supporting internal and external sales.

The successful candidate will have enough technical experience to be able to independently manage various sized field efforts and deliver associated reports for a wide variety of hazardous building material projects/surveys and industrial hygiene projects. They should possess strong interpersonal and communication abilities to effectively engage with team members, clients, and stakeholders. This candidate will be committed to the team’s success and growth; will rigorously apply safety policies and procedures; and will effectively manage the quality of field efforts and project deliverables within the bounds of AECOM’s Quality Management System. This position calls for excellent organization and time management skills, flexibility to work on a multitude of diverse projects, a positive attitude, and a willingness to support the mentorship and growth of staff.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

BA/BS + 8 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and or education.
Technical experience directly related to building hazardous material (asbestos, lead paint, etc.)
Industrial hygiene, mold, or indoor air quality experience.
Must have 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training.
Must have EPA AHERA Asbestos Inspector Certification.
Must have New England State specific licenses and certifications pertaining to asbestos (MA, ME, NH, CT) or be eligible to obtain such licenses and certifications.
Valid Driver’s License and must be able to pass AECOM’s Motor Vehicle Records review.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with strategy and growth plan development and execution

Experience managing and/or mentoring a team of technical professionals
Experience managing small to large size public and private sector projects
Experience managing scope and budget, and staff administration and development
Experience building client relationships, business development and client management
Highly effective verbal and written communication skills; extremely proficient in technical writing; highly effective organization and multi-tasking skills.
Internally driven, self-starter, team oriented

Additional Information

Relocation is not available for this position
Sponsorship is not available for this position
Willing to travel out-of-town for durations ranging from approximately one week to three months, as needed. Travel will vary greatly and depend on the workload/projects at any given time.

About the Company
Persistent Systems is a leading global technology company dedicated to delivering innovative software solutions and digital transformation services. With a strong focus on healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and other critical industries, Persistent Systems leverages cutting-edge technologies to help organizations optimize their operations, improve patient outcomes, and achieve strategic goals. The company prides itself on fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and dynamic work environment that nurtures talent and promotes continuous learning. With a commitment to excellence and integrity, Persistent Systems has established a reputation for delivering high-quality solutions tailored to client needs across the globe.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Data Analyst specializing in healthcare data to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will possess strong expertise in MS SQL, healthcare data modeling, data integration, and statistical analysis. In this role, you will play a key part in building scalable cloud infrastructure, implementing system health monitoring, and developing continuous integration pipelines. Your insights will support critical healthcare initiatives such as value-based care, population health, and operational efficiency. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze large healthcare datasets, create comprehensive reports, and develop data workflows that drive strategic decision-making. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work with state-of-the-art technologies in a fast-paced, innovative environment, contributing to impactful healthcare projects.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Healthcare Analytics, or a related field. A minimum of 7 years of hands-on experience working with US healthcare datasets, including claims, benefits, and eligibility data, is essential. Proficiency in SQL for querying and analyzing complex healthcare data is required, along with familiarity with modern data warehousing platforms such as Snowflake and MySQL. Experience in creating healthcare process flows and data documentation using tools like Microsoft Visio or draw.io is highly desirable. Candidates should demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to validate and transform data accurately. Excellent communication skills are necessary to effectively collaborate with technical teams and non-technical stakeholders, translating complex data insights into clear, actionable reports.

Responsibilities
As a Data Analyst in Healthcare at Persistent Systems, your responsibilities will include analyzing large-scale healthcare datasets, including claims, provider, utilization, and quality metrics. You will write and optimize complex SQL queries to extract, validate, and analyze healthcare data from relational databases, ensuring data accuracy and integrity. Supporting data validation, reconciliation, and transformation processes will be vital to meet business and regulatory reporting requirements. You will work closely with data engineering teams to support the ingestion and integration of data from various source systems such as claims processing platforms, provider databases, and eligibility feeds. Developing and maintaining healthcare data models, marts, and analytics layers on platforms like Snowflake and MySQL will be a core part of your role. You will also create process maps, data lineage diagrams, and system architecture visuals to document healthcare workflows, business rules, and metrics definitions. Collaborating with stakeholders across healthcare operations, finance, clinical, quality, and compliance teams, you will translate complex healthcare data into clear insights, presenting findings and recommendations to leadership and cross-functional teams. Additionally, you will support analytics initiatives aimed at improving healthcare quality, operational efficiency, and population health outcomes.

Benefits
Persistent Systems offers a competitive salary package complemented by comprehensive benefits designed to support our employees' well-being and professional growth. Our culture emphasizes talent development, providing quarterly growth opportunities, and sponsoring higher education and certification programs. Employees benefit from working with cutting-edge technologies and engaging in innovative projects. We foster a vibrant work environment with engagement initiatives such as team-building events, flexible work hours, and recognition programs like Long Service awards. Annual health check-ups and insurance coverage—including group term life, personal accident, and Mediclaim hospitalization for employees and their families—are provided to ensure health and security. Our commitment to work-life balance and continuous development makes Persistent Systems an ideal place for ambitious professionals to thrive and advance their careers.

Equal Opportunity (in last)
Persistent Systems is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, regardless of gender, gender identity, or ethnicity. We support hybrid work arrangements and flexible hours to accommodate diverse lifestyles. Our facilities are accessible and equipped with ergonomic setups and assistive technologies to support employees with physical disabilities. If you have specific requirements, please inform us during the application process or at any point during your employment. We believe that diversity and inclusion drive innovation and excellence, and we are dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can succeed.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Credit Risk
jobs.description:
Experience in credit risk analytics, ECL and loss forecasting experience, alongside SQL skills and the confidence to influence senior stakeholders
Own and shape Zip’s ECL and loss forecasting processes, turning complex credit risk data into insights that influence important business decisions
Work flexibly in a hybrid role from our Sydney or Melbourne office

Write your story with a career at Zip

With a broad remit across credit risk strategy and decisioning, forecasting, portfolio analytics and controls monitoring, our Risk Management & Data Science team is a key strategic interface between the business and a varied range of internal and external stakeholders.

Working with world class platforms and given the freedom to experiment and uplift your analytical and modelling capabilities, you’ll be a part of a flat structure and a close knit team responsible for improving the commercials related to arrears and repayments.

As a Senior Data Analyst in Credit Risk Management, you’ll take end to end ownership of Zip’s Expected Credit Loss and loss forecasting processes. You’ll connect portfolio performance with ECL, losses and forward looking forecasts, while continually improving the quality, automation and explainability of our approach.

This is an opportunity to combine deep analytical thinking with meaningful stakeholder influence, partnering closely with Credit Risk, Finance and Data to turn complex movements into clear insights and recommendations.

What You’ll Own

Own the monthly ECL operating cycle and loss forecasting process, delivering accurate, timely and explainable outcomes
Lead quarterly ECL parameter monitoring, investigating material movements and connecting changes in portfolio performance with expected loss outcomes
Continuously improve the ECL production code base, automation, controls, repeatability and turnaround times
Strengthen data governance and controls, identifying data quality issues early and partnering with our Data team to resolve them
Lead regular ECL discussions with senior Credit Risk and Finance stakeholders, translating complex analysis into clear insights, decisions and actions
Own the methodology, assumptions, scenario analysis and variance analysis underpinning loss forecasts, continually looking for opportunities to improve forecast accuracy
Lead the annual ECL review, including methodology and performance assessments, back testing, documentation and support for internal and external audit activity
Explore how AI and new technology can make our forecasting and analytical processes faster, smarter and more effective
Provide analytical support for bad debt sale initiatives and other emerging Credit Risk priorities

What You'll Bring To The Team

Zipsters work on a broad range of initiatives, and our skills and experiences all look a little different. What really matters to us is that you’re a great fit with our four Values, and have a desire to learn and grow.

So whether you meet some or all of the desirable attributes below, we’d still love to hear from you:

Experience in credit risk analytics within retail banking, consumer finance or another regulated financial services environment
Strong experience in credit loss forecasting or portfolio loss analytics, with the ability to connect portfolio performance, delinquency and write offs with expected loss outcomes
Practical experience with ECL, including PD, LGD and EAD, impairment processes and credit risk parameter monitoring
Strong SQL skills and experience maintaining analytical code, with exposure to Python, R or SAS highly regarded
A disciplined approach to data quality, testing, controls, documentation and production change management
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the confidence to explain analytical outcomes, challenge assumptions and lead discussions with senior stakeholders
The ability to translate complex analysis into clear recommendations that support effective decision making
A mindset that embraces AI and new tools to adapt, learn and grow.
An aptitude for identifying and managing risks. Whether you are a People Manager or an Individual Contributor, we are all leaders at Zip, therefore effective risk management is important to how we run our business and part of all our roles.
Our values in your DNA: Customer First, Own It, Stronger Together and Change the Game

What You’ll Get In Return

As we write this next exciting chapter in our story, we will continue to move at pace and embrace change. For you, this might mean opportunities to learn new skills with hands-on experience, broader responsibilities, or the buzz of seeing your work impact customers faster.

Zip is a place where you’ll get out exactly what you put in. When you join the team, we'll do our best to make sure you can be yourself and surround yourself with smart, friendly colleagues and leaders who have your back, so that you can make the big things happen.

Zipsters tell us these are just some of the best things about working here. You’ll also receive:

25 days paid leave annually, including birthday leave and quarterly wellbeing days
16 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers, and 4 weeks for supporting carers
Family support policies including miscarriage bereavement leave and domestic violence leave
Mental health and wellness initiatives, including $299 annual wellbeing allowance, free access for you and family members to our EAP service Sonder, discounted private health insurance, and great rates on fitness sessions through ClassPass
2 days paid volunteering leave per year
Access to the Flare Benefits Hub and Novated Leasing for savings across lifestyle, essentials and wellbeing
Fee-free Zip products, and discounts with Zip merchant partners
Team social events, epic offices, free breakfast daily, and weekly free lunches

Be a part of a team that reflects the diversity of our customers

We pride ourselves on being a workplace that provides equal opportunities to people of all ages, cultural backgrounds, sexual orientations, gender identities, abilities, veteran status, and everything else that makes you unique.

Equally, we’re committed to ensuring our recruitment processes are accessible and inclusive. Please let us know If there are any adjustments that need to be made to ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

And finally…get to know us

Zip Co Limited (ASX: ZIP) is a digital financial services company, offering innovative, people-centred products that bring customers and merchants together.

Operating in two core markets - Australia and the US, Zip offers point-of-sale credit and digital payment services, connecting millions of customers with its global network of tens of thousands of merchants.

We’re proud to be a values-led business and our values - Customer First, Own it, Stronger Together and Change the Game - guide us in everything we do.

About The Company

DiDi Global Inc. is the world’s leading mobility technology platform. It offers a wide range of app-based services across markets including Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa, including ride hailing, taxi hailing, chauffeur, hitch and other forms of shared mobility as well as auto solutions, food delivery, intra-city freight, and financial services.

DiDi provides car owners, drivers, and delivery partners with flexible work and income opportunities. It is committed to collaborating with policymakers, the taxi industry, the automobile industry and the communities to solve the world’s transportation, environmental and employment challenges through the use of AI technology and localized smart transportation innovations. DiDi strives to create better life experiences and greater social value, by building a safe, inclusive and sustainable transportation and local services ecosystem for cities of the future.

For more information, please visit: www.didiglobal.com/news

About The Team/role

We are looking for a Data Analyst to support our Fintech line of business in Mexico. This role is critical in enabling localized insights and supporting operational execution through data. You will partner closely with regional team of Engagement to help drive key initiatives that serve our customers in Mexico.

In this role, you'll be...

Participate in business analysis efforts for Mexico’s credit card product
Translate local market dynamics into actionable insights by analyzing customer behavior, product performance, and financial metrics.
Collaborate with stakeholders in the credit card Engagement Operation team to support go-to-market strategies, product enhancements, and regulatory initiatives
Monitor and report on key business metrics through dashboards and performance reviews tailored to the Mexican market.
Ensure data accuracy and consistency by aligning with data engineering and governance teams.

We're eager to be in touch because you have...

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Statistics, or related field.
1+ years of experience in business analysis or analytics, preferably in fintech or financial services.
Solid command of SQL and Python, along with a proactive attitude toward learning new technologies and coding languages as needed.
Experience in product performance tracking, financial modeling, and decision support is preferred
Fluency in English.

You'll love working at DiDi because...

We create user value

We strive to always create valuable experiences for our users in everything we do. Our focus is to always innovate new experiences that are safe, pleasant and efficient.

We are data-driven

We are strong believers in making informed decisions, that’s why we are data-driven. We can better navigate the business landscape strategically by analyzing valuable metrics.

Win-win Collaboration

Success is a team sport. When we work to help our partners and colleagues win, we win, too. While keeping everyone's best interest at heart, we communicate with candor and execute with excellence in all we do.

We believe in integrity

Integrity is at the very core of our business. We are people who always want to do the right thing. Our intentions are sincere, we speak our minds and listen to each other.

Growth

We always strive to do better. That means venturing beyond our comfort zones, learning from our mistakes, and helping each other grow.

Diversity and Inclusion

Diversity is one of our biggest strengths. Our differences are what make us distinct. We respect each other and believe in equal opportunities for all.

We are committed to building inclusive and diverse teams

At DiDi, we believe that our differences are our biggest source of strength. That’s why we are committed to promoting equal opportunities to all candidates and employees as an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Employment and advancement decisions at DiDi are always made based on the needs of the position and the qualifications of the candidate. We do not discriminate against any employee or applicant based on their gender, age, sexual orientation, nationality, marital status, pregnancy/maternity, disability, race, religion and beliefs, or any other status protected by applicable laws wherever we operate.

We are committed to building inclusive and diverse teams, and a workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment, because that’s how we create better products and services, make better decisions and better serve the communities we’re a part of.

Als Business Analyst ben je verantwoordelijk voor het analyseren, structureren en visualiseren van data. Je ontwikkelt rapportages en dashboards die bijdragen aan betere prestaties, hogere datakwaliteit en strategische besluitvorming.

Analyseren van operationele, logistieke en financiële data en signaleren van trends
Adviseren van management op basis van data gedreven inzichten en analyses
