jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
About Annalect

As every CMO knows, employing technology, data and analytics to business challenges is the cost of entry, not a nice to have. Unlocking the value of consumer data can deliver growth, revenue, and ROI, and create differentiation to stay on top. Real-time action is instrumental in driving results within a highly fragmented marketplace.

Annalect is the data and technology division of Omnicom. We provide a variety of services to our clients and media agency partners. As a company, we serve as the foundational data and technology layer in which analytics and insights can be accessed through a single lens. Our main goal is to advance the advertising and marketing strategies of our clients with applications that unlock insights and drive business results.

Annalect is a global data, technology, and analytics consultancy, with a strong footprint in the APAC region with offices in Bangalore, Gurgaon, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Melbourne, Singapore and Sydney. We create solutions across data, measurement, analytics, visualisation, and marketing technology to maximise the effectiveness of media and our client’s media ROI.

Annalect’s unique approach to data and technology – one that relies on transparency, neutrality, and interoperability – allows us to deliver purpose-built and scalable solutions that make data actionable. We have teams of analysts, data scientists, consultants, and technical experts to help us meet the business goals of our agency partners and clients.
Join our dynamic and diverse team at Annalect -- data solutions for marketers, by marketers.

As a Data Analyst on the Annalect team, you will be tasked with aiding in the transformation of vast data sets into compelling and actionable insights.
You will work directly with other analysts and consultants in BI Visualization team, as well as client and agency teams, to communicate your findings and build strategies around them.

Day-to-day:

Build and maintaining dashboards using visualization tools such as Datorama, Data Studio and others
Working closely with stakeholders (both internal and external) to centralise high-quality data from various sources.
Assess quality of data through various techniques.
Work on regular report delivery around media and advertising updates.
Communicate data insights and outliers through impactful data visualisation and storytelling.

Responsibilities:

Build and maintain dashboards and reports
Build and maintain taxonomy via Excel or in house tool for various media channels to ensure correct data collection
Provide support and maintenance of dashboards to ensure availability and performance of developed reports and dashboards; Working with Data Governance teams to build data checks to constantly improve the data integrity and accuracy of dashboards
Work with the Manager and the agency teams to execute advanced analytics and data science needs, around but not limited to ad tech field e.g. Web/app analytics solutions, attribution study
Build reports and provides analysis to existing and new projects via third-party media platforms and analytics tools
Generating and communicating clear, compelling and actionable insights
Ensuring that client facing and internal reporting is done in a timely manner
Presenting reports to clients during monthly and weekly phone calls

Key skills:

Knowledge and experience of visualization tools such as Datorama, Data Studio, Power BI, etc is preferred
Knowledge in key advertising channels e.g. GMP, Facebook, other DSPs
Strong data processing & data visualization skills
Knowledge of 1 or more of: Python, R, SQL
Analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills
Effective communicator with well-developed written and verbal skills, ideally in the media industry

Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in statistics, mathematics, economics, engineering, information management, social sciences or business/marketing related fields.
Basic knowledge in data analytics and visualization area (Datorama, Data Studio, Power BI etc)
Experience in either SQL, Python, R
Familiarity with SAS, SPSS, R or other advanced analytics software packages is a plus
Ability to manipulate and troubleshoot large data sets
A strong desire to learn and passion for both performance marketing and analytics
Ability to manage and prioritize a number of concurrent tasks
Ability to clearly explain complex technical ideas to multiple audiences both verbally and in writing
Ability to work well with others and work in cross functional teams
Expertise in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint is a requirement for the role
Prior agency experience is a plus
Familiar with advertising channels and platforms: Facebook, Google Ads, DV360 and others
Familiarity with at least some of the following tools: marketing technology (e.g. Data Management Platforms), ad-serving (e.g. Google DCM, Atlas), web analytics (e.g. Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics), social (e.g. Facebook Insights, Twitter Insights, Crimson Hexagon)
Detail oriented and good organizational skills

jobs.title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence.

Backed by a $122M USD Series D funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

We are excited to meet with qualified candidates and are grateful for everyone’s interest. Please note that this is a hybrid position (2x a week) requiring applicants to be within driving distance of Toronto.

The Opportunity

That's where you come in. We're looking for a passionate, resourceful, and driven Sales Enablement Program Manager to help our Go-to-Market teams ramp faster, grow their skills, and perform at their best.

This role is ideal for someone who loves learning, enjoys helping others develop, and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. You'll play a key role in improving onboarding, delivering engaging training, building scalable enablement programs, and partnering with leaders across the business to drive performance.

You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships, Product Marketing, Product, and Revenue Operations to ensure our teams have the knowledge, tools, and resources they need to succeed.

What You’ll Be Doing

Onboarding & Learning Programs

Support and continuously improve onboarding programs across our Go-to-Market organization.
Manage and maintain learning paths within our LMS (Workramp), ensuring content remains current, engaging, and effective.
Update onboarding and training materials by applying feedback, lessons learned, and evolving business needs.
Partner with subject matter experts to develop and enhance learning content.

Training & Facilitation

Deliver engaging live onboarding sessions, workshops, certifications, and ongoing training.
Support the planning and execution of monthly enablement programs and learning initiatives.
Facilitate interactive learning experiences that encourage participation and knowledge retention.

Program Management

Design, rollout, and continuous improvement of enablement programs.
Coordinate cross-functional projects with stakeholders across Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Product, and Revenue Operations.
Create and maintain enablement resources including playbooks, guides, job aids, and training materials.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

Track onboarding progress, certifications, participation, and enablement program effectiveness (Tableau Dashboard & Gong Dashboards, Workramp Reports).
Analyze feedback and performance metrics to identify opportunities for improvement.
Share insights and recommendations with leaders to continually evolve our enablement strategy.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you'll help create an exceptional onboarding experience, deliver impactful learning programs, build trusted relationships across the business, and continuously improve how we enable our Go-to-Market teams. Your work will directly contribute to faster ramp times, stronger adoption of key initiatives, and continuous development of higher-performing teams.

What You Offer Blue J

3+ years of experience in Sales Enablement Program Manager, Learning & Development, or a similar enablement role.
Previous experience in a customer-facing GTM role such as: Business Development Representative (BDR/SDR), Account Executive, Account Manager, and Partnerships Representative.
Passionate about learning and helping others grow. You're a true learner at heart and are energized by helping others succeed.
Resourceful, proactive, and driven. You take initiative, seek out solutions, and are always looking for ways to improve programs and the learner experience.
Adaptable and comfortable with change. You thrive in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve, new initiatives emerge, and continuous improvement is part of the culture.
Solid presentation, facilitation, and communication skills.
Excellent organization and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.
Comfortable collaborating with stakeholders across different teams and levels of the organization.
Detail-oriented while keeping the bigger picture in mind.
Comfortable using data, feedback, and insights to measure success and continuously improve enablement programs.
Comfortable leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to drive efficiency, improve workflows, and stay ahead of industry trends.

Nice to Have

Experience with an LMS (WorkRamp is a plus).
Experience building out enablement programs.
Familiarity with tools such as Gong, Salesforce, Notion, Google Workspace, or similar GTM technologies.

What We Offer You

The opportunity to shape how our Go-to-Market teams learn, ramp, and perform, to support BlueJ as we scale.
A mission-driven culture where your work directly advances clarity, efficiency, and accessibility in tax research.
Competitive base salary, stock options, and benefits designed to support you and your family.
A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive team that values innovation, respect, and fun.
The excitement of a fast-growing, well-funded company with clear momentum, and the resources to back bold initiatives.

The Core Values that Define Our Culture

We are customer-focused
We put team over self
We are pleasant and playful
We are open to better ideas
We move fast and fix things

What To Expect In The Interview Process

We anticipate a high volume of applicants for this role and are excited to grow our team. A human will review each application and get back to you as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you!

Interview Process

Step 1: Chat with Bailey, our Talent Acquisition Manager
Step 2: Meet with Jamie, Manager of GTM Enablement
Step 3: Present your case study to Jamie, Manager of GTM Enablement, Alex, Business Development Manager, and an additional stakeholder based on availability
Step 4: Wrap up with Ben, our CEO

We believe our strength is built on diversity of thought, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. We value inclusiveness and are an equal opportunity employer. About The Role

We're partnering with the world's leading AI research labs to build the next generation of AI-powered security operations tools. As a Security Operations Analyst, you'll bring your real-world SOC experience to help train and evaluate AI systems that reason through security incidents, alerts, and investigations — ensuring they reflect how skilled analysts actually work.

Work on cutting-edge AI projects in partnership with top security and AI research teams
Fully remote and flexible — work on your schedule, at your own pace
Freelance perks: autonomy, variety, and global collaboration
Make a tangible impact on how AI systems handle real-world cybersecurity challenges
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension

About The Role

We're partnering with the world's leading AI research teams to build the next generation of intelligent security systems — and we need experienced security practitioners to help us get there.

As a Network & Infrastructure Security Analyst, you'll bring your real-world expertise to bear on a genuinely meaningful challenge: helping AI understand how threats, controls, and failures interact in production enterprise environments. Group Investments are currently seeking a Senior Investment Operations Analyst to be based in New York. Working collaboratively with trade desks and external partners globally to ensure GI’s trade life cycle is managed and supported across all locations in a timely and efficient manner. Minimized instances of trades failing.

Supporting both internal and external audit processes to enable accurate and effective assessment of controls and activities.
Engagement and collaboration with key stakeholders to determine key areas of improvement in existing processes.

jobs.description:
We recognize our competitive advantage -- our people. We believe in our people, who share our vision of meeting the needs of our employees, customers, and communities and who carry out the continued success of the company.

Our employees are committed to the company's foundational values: integrity, excellence, teamwork, environmental stewardship, and community commitment. In turn, we invest in our employees, providing opportunities for challenge and advancement and offering a competitive compensation package.

Applications will be screened based on the information provided; in order to assist us in determining qualifications, please upload a current resume and take some time to update your employment information, certifications, etc. The information will flow over to your profile.

Posting End Date: This position will remain open until filled. Early applications are highly encouraged.

BRIEF POSTING DESCRIPTION:

The P PD PROGRAM MANAGEMENT Department of the P INVESTMENT PLANNING & STRATEGY Division at Hawaiian Electric Company has 1 Management vacancy available. (Role: Professional).This posting seeks to fill at either the Project Manager or Senior Project Manager; whichever level is most suited to the qualifications of the applying candidate.

PROJECT MANAGER

JOB FUNCTION:

Responsible for planning, organizing, and managing scope, schedule, and costs for Energy Delivery projects and programs requiring complex regulatory approvals, land/Right-of-Way acquisition, public relations management, or cross-functional/multilevel (internal) management from conceptualization/inception through budgeting, design, approval, procurement, construction, placement in operation, and project closing. Serves as a focal point for all project/program matters and is responsible for meeting all project related objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Working closely with Supervisor and Sr. Project Managers:

Plans, organizes, and manages all project and/or program tasks associated with scoping, budgeting, design, approval, procurement, construction, placement in operation, and closing of projects. Provides project leadership and work direction and secures commitment from team members in meeting project milestones. Ensures team members have all resources, information, and direction necessary to successfully perform their jobs. Evaluates progress and performance of team members and implements personnel actions necessary to accomplish objectives including recognition, redirection, recruitment, and replacement of team members.
Serves as the focal point for all programs/projects related matters. Works with and through community groups, neighborhood boards, government agencies, the media, other utilities and private companies, the City Council, the State Legislature, and the PUC to disseminate information, address concerns, obtain permits and approvals, and resolve project-related problems. Prepares and provides testimonies and presentations at internal strategic meetings, public meetings, and regulatory hearings as necessary.
Develops necessary strategies required to meet program/project goals. Makes early identification of potential problem areas. Solves problems to ensure attainment of program/project goals. Redirects planning, design, purchasing, permits/approvals or construction to prevent or minimize constraints or actions which may delay schedules or add costs to programs and projects in construction. Conducts inspections of construction sites as necessary.
Develops and maintains program/project schedules. Prepares and presents program/project progress and cost reports internally and externally as required.
Works with Regulatory Affairs, Budgets, Management Accounting & Financial Services, Community Relations, Government Relations, Corporate Communications, Legal, Energy Delivery departments, and others in obtaining approvals. Obtains Company authorizations for expenditures for funds for engineering, materials, and construction. Reviews and approves procurement for program permitting, design, material, and construction and for project material and construction.
Participates in Company emergency response activities as assigned, including any activities required to prepare for such emergency response.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Knowledge Requirements

Advanced knowledge of project management principles, and engineering and construction practices in the transmission and distribution and/or generation fields, normally acquired through college-level training and/or equivalent experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification from a nationally recognized organization such as the Project Management Institute (PMI), a plus.
Working knowledge of personal computers and related software applications such as MS Project, UI Planner, Ellipse/DARS, Microsoft Word, Excel, SAP etc.
Knowledge of LEAN continuous improvement principles and best practices to achieve operational excellence.
Knowledge of basic Safety principles and best practices to achieve a safe workplace environment.

Skills Requirements

Excellent written, oral and presentation skills.
Strong interpersonal skills to direct, influence, motivate and persuade various groups or individuals.
Ability to handle difficult and/or sensitive issues while using tact, courtesy, and discretion.
Able to work with a variety of individuals occasionally dealing with sensitive, difficult, or confrontational issues and the ability to handle such issues with professionalism by using tact, courtesy, respect and discretion.
In-depth analytical, computational, organizational, and time-management skills to handle various projects.
Ability to work collaboratively as a member of a team.
Ability to manage people at all levels within the company.
Ability to develop/maintain strong positive relationships with leaders and members of the community and government.
Ability to remain flexible in a demanding work environment and adapt to rapidly changing priorities and strategic direction. Ability to conceptualize new ideas quickly.
Must have or be able to qualify for a State of Hawaii driver’s license. Must meet the standards for driving positions stated in the Hiring Standards for Driving Positions policy. These standards may be adjusted periodically to meet business and safety objectives.

Experience Requirements

Several (3-5 years) experience as a project manager, construction manager, designer, engineer, or in a project support position that involved hands on experience with small to medium scale projects, preferably within the electric utility industry. A degree in a related field may be substituted for three (3)-years of experience.
Few (1-3) years of project management experience for small to large engineering/construction projects.
Experience with the regulatory, social, public affairs (neighborhood boards, community groups, government agencies, political leaders, media, etc.) processes involved with land use issues.
Few (1-3) years of leadership experience is desirable.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Water Conveyance
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're driven by a shared purpose—to deliver innovative, technically excellent water infrastructure solutions that strengthen our communities. As a Water Conveyance Project Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to lead complex and meaningful conveyance projects, shape long-term client relationships, and influence the growth of our regional water practice. This role offers the autonomy to lead, the support to succeed, and the career runway to make a lasting impact.

As a Water Conveyance Project Manager, you’ll be charged with leading a team of highly qualified and motivated engineers through the design process, interacting directly with clients to develop and deliver technical conveyance solutions, and mentoring ambitious mid-level engineers. We’ll ask you to grow your career by acting as a highly competent seller-doer that will be empowered to develop and manage projects in a trusting and supported environment.

You’ll serve as a Project Manager/Design Manager leading a technical team, performing technical tasks, and coordinating the use of resources to accomplish multiple, concurrent water infrastructure projects. Your responsibilities may include planning and design related management and technical support roles for various types of conveyance systems such as open channel flow and low-pressure conduit, flow control structures, and pump stations and force mains. Additional assignments may include other water-related civil infrastructure evaluations. You’ll have the opportunity to grow professionally through participation on project teams delivering challenging projects while serving and developing clients.

You’ll be asked to support business development activities in order to grow the local conveyance group. You’ll work with key clients resulting in acquisition of new projects as well as perform the role of Project Manager supporting various projects and programs within a defined client portfolio. You’ll effectively lead and manage project teams throughout all phases of project planning, execution, and closeout; consistent with established project delivery processes to meet the scope, schedule, budget, and other specified requirements stated in each contract.

Using your conveyance technical expertise, you’ll play an integral role in leading and mentoring staff, forming long-term relationships with clients and pursuing new work, building water client portfolios, including strategy development, positioning, proposing, and negotiating contracts. You’ll help others discover what drives them, nurturing their purpose and guiding them forward. Your role will keep our company connected, and we’ll support you with what you need to be successful. But you’re not just a leader – you’re an achiever.  

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's Degree in Civil, Mechanical, and/or Environmental Engineering.
Registration as a Professional Engineer (PE) is required or ability to obtain.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive civil engineering experience.
Demonstrated ability to manage scope, budget, schedule, and technical quality across complex infrastructure projects.

Ideally, you’ll also have

A Master's degree in Civil Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Experience serving various clients involving a wide variety of fields including conveyance pipeline design, project management, water/wastewater pump station design.
Demonstrated ability to lead the design and preparation of plans, specifications, estimates, studies, proposals and/or reports.
Experience with Design-Build and/or EPC projects.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $145,000.00 to $195,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on August 25, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

Position Summary:

jobs.title: Sales Development Program Manager
jobs.description:
Description

AEM (Advanced Environmental Monitoring) is the global leader in innovative mission critical weather, wildfire and water monitoring and intelligence solutions. We aim to be the world’s essential source for environmental insights – enabling decisive action and positive outcomes for our customers and their constituents. Our family of innovators offers world-class hydrometeorological technologies and services, including sensors, dataloggers, telemetry, and advanced analytics and software. Our technology and services empower the communities and organizations to survive – and thrive – in the face of escalating environmental risks.

We're hiring a Sales Development Program Manager to own AEM's outbound prospecting function end to end. This is the singular headcount responsible for top-of-funnel pipeline across our commercial verticals, and the person in this seat will build the system, run it, and continuously improve it.

This is a player-coach role. You will run outbound sequences yourself, set sales calls, and optimize what's working, while also building the Apollo automation, AI tooling, and process infrastructure that allows the function to scale. We're looking for someone who already uses AI as a core part of their daily prospecting workflow, not someone who plans to learn it.

Job Responsibilities

Outbound pipeline and prospecting

Own and hit a monthly quota of outbound attended meetings and qualified opportunities across AEM's priority verticals.
Run multi-channel outbound cadences across email, phone, and LinkedIn, working named target accounts with 3-5 contacts per account before moving on.
Identify the right contacts at the right accounts using intent signals, website visitor data, job posting triggers, and seasonal market timing.
Follow up on inbound leads with urgency, enroll them into the right sequences, and hand off qualified meetings to the sales team with clean context.

Apollo automation and AI-assisted prospecting

Own the Apollo instance as AEM's primary outbound operating system, including the sequence library, list hygiene, sending infrastructure, and performance reporting.
Build and continuously optimize AI-assisted prospecting workflows using tools like Claude and ChatGPT to produce sequence copy, call scripts, and account research at scale.
Convert manual sequence steps to automated where quality allows, and maintain clean domain health and list quality to protect sender reputation.
Run a structured weekly review of sequence performance: reply rates, bounce rates, subject line tests, and contact enrollment, and act on what the data says.

ABM and market development

Build and manage intent-based target account lists tied to seasonal events, weather triggers, geography, and ICP fit, and keep them fresh.
Coordinate with marketing on campaign-aligned outbound plays, webinar follow-up, and content-driven sequences.
Bring new top-of-funnel ideas: new verticals, new triggers, new channels. This function is being built from scratch and you have the latitude to shape it.

This job description may not be inclusive of all assigned duties, responsibilities, or aspects of the job described, and may be amended at any time at the sole discretion of the Employer.

Requirements

3 to 5 years of SDR, BDR, or outbound sales experience in a B2B environment with a track record of consistently hitting meeting and pipeline goals.
Hands-on sequencing platform experience in Apollo or an equivalent tool: you have built sequences, managed lists, and read performance data, not just enrolled contacts in someone else's cadence.
Multi-channel cadence execution in practice: email, phone, and LinkedIn working together, with LinkedIn and calling as real parts of the motion, not afterthoughts.
Working experience using AI writing and research tools as part of a daily prospecting workflow: Claude, ChatGPT, or similar. This is a hard requirement, not a nice to have.
Comfortable reading sequence and campaign performance data and making decisions from it. You know the difference between an activity problem and a conversion problem.
Clear, direct written communication. Your cold emails sound like a person, not a template. You can write something under 50 words that actually gets a reply.
Experience or genuine interest in environmental technology, weather monitoring, energy, government, or industrial markets is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Additional Information

This is a remote opportunity that can be done from anywhere in the continental United States and/or Canada
Must be eligible to work in the U.S. or Canada without company sponsorship, now or in the future, for employment-based work authorization. F-1 visa holders with Optional Practical Training (OPT) who will require H-1B status, TNs, or current H-1B visa holders will not be considered. H1-B and green card sponsorship is not available for this position.

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Risk PMO team protects Stripe’s revenue and drives cross-functional strategy for company-level and org-level priorities. As Stripe operates across an increasingly complex and fast-moving global regulatory environment, one of our most important functions is ensuring that our largest, most strategic users can grow with us—compliantly, confidently, and at speed.

We sit at the intersection of Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and GTM—serving as the bridge between teams coordinating massive programs with global, wide-reaching impact. We build durable systems that enable strong collaboration across functions and seamless experiences for our users.

If you're energized by high-stakes, ambiguous problems and thrive on building programs from scratch in environments where the rules are still being written—we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

You will define, own, and execute program strategies for large-scale regulatory initiatives, operating with significant autonomy across a portfolio of global projects.

This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor (IC) role. While you will influence senior leadership and set strategic direction, you are also the primary driver of execution. You will need to zoom out to design the long-term vision, and zoom in to manage the details—building templates, tracking deliverables, writing documentation, and directly unblocking cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

Own and execute high-stakes global programs end-to-end, from initial strategy and scoping to project planning, day-to-day tracking, and change management
Drive step-change improvements in our operational processes, rolling up your sleeves to build systems and workflows that directly improve business outcomes and top-line metrics
Bridge compliance and commercial strategy by partnering with GTM and account leadership to turn complex regulatory requirements into a competitive advantage that builds deep user trust
Build and run operating models across diverse cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance), keeping highly distributed workstreams aligned and accountable
Serve as a trusted advisor by preparing strategic reviews for senior stakeholders and managing critical escalations
Translate user friction into program evolution by establishing structured, data-driven approaches to gather user feedback and turning those insights into actionable product and operational improvements
Diagnose and resolve systemic operational gaps before they impact our users, building self-healing processes and scalable internal infrastructure
Champion Stripe’s Operating Principles by fostering a high-performance culture that values rigorous thinking, rapid execution, and putting users first

Who you are

You are a highly strategic operator, a masterful communicator, and a systems thinker with operational grit. You thrive in the gray area, possessing the ability to translate ambiguous global challenges into elegant, structured, and highly actionable operational frameworks.

You are a natural leader who leads by influence and by example. You have a deep empathy for the user, an unyielding bias toward action, and you take pride in the craft of execution. No problem is too complex for you to deconstruct, and no detail is too small if it impacts the user experience.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of experience in Program Management, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, or Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
Hands-on execution track record: Proven ability to work independently as an individual contributor, managing complex, multi-stakeholder project plans and deliverables from inception to completion
Exceptional communication & storytelling: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to distill highly complex, technical, or regulatory topics into clear, succinct, and persuasive narratives to external and senior audiences
Systems and infrastructure builder: Deep experience designing, launching, and scaling complex cross-functional operating models, feedback loops, and PMO frameworks
Growth mindset: A high willingness to learn, adapt quickly to changing environments, and actively seek and act on feedback to continuously improve

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in high-growth technology or fintech environments
Deep cross-functional partnership: Prior experience working alongside Engineering, Product, Legal, Compliance, and GTM/Sales
Data fluency: Experience leveraging data visualization tools and analytical frameworks to back up strategic decisions and measure program success

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

jobs.title: Tolling Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview

Kimley-Horn is seeking a Business Analyst
to support its growing tolling, managed lanes, and transportation technology practice in Pleasanton, CA. This role will help translate toll agency operations, policies, business rules, and system needs into clear requirements, workflows, documentation, and implementation support for projects involving roadside toll systems, back-office systems, customer service operations, inventory management, maintenance and operations systems, and emerging tolling technologies.

The ideal candidate will bring hands-on business analysis experience, strong stakeholder facilitation skills, and a practical understanding of tolling operations. The position is intended for a professional who can work across technical, operational, and client-facing teams to support requirements development, configuration alignment, operational readiness, testing, and successful project delivery.

Responsibilities

Support tolling business analysis activities for roadway, roadside, operational back-office, commercial back-office, customer service, MOMS, inventory, and interoperability-related projects.
Lead or assist with requirements elicitation, validation, clarification, and traceability, including development and maintenance of Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs).
Document current-state and future-state business processes, workflows, business rules, service blueprints, user stories, use cases, and operational procedures.
Coordinate with toll agencies, project managers, system integrators, operations teams, engineers, QA teams, vendors, and other stakeholders to confirm that business needs are accurately reflected in project deliverables.
Support development and review of configuration workbooks, business rules, policy interpretations, system settings, and operational assumptions to confirm alignment with client requirements and day-to-day operating needs.
Assist with back-office and roadside tolling system implementation efforts, including account management, billing, invoicing, payments, transponder/tag management, image review, violations, dispute handling, reconciliation, and customer correspondence workflows.
Support system testing, user acceptance testing, business validation, demonstrations, release planning, go-live readiness, and post-implementation support activities.
Analyze operational impacts, risks, process gaps, and customer-experience considerations associated with new system features, technology changes, or operational transitions.
Prepare clear business documentation, meeting notes, process maps, requirements packages, test support materials, decision logs, issue summaries, training materials, and other project artifacts consistent with client and Kimley-Horn standards.
Contribute to tolling advisory, system manager, procurement support, concepts of operations, business rule development, and operational readiness assignments as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, transportation, engineering, public administration, finance, or a related field.
Minimum of 7 years of business analysis, systems analysis, transportation operations, tolling, back-office, customer service, financial operations, or related consulting experience.
Experience gathering, documenting, validating, and managing business requirements for technology-enabled operations or public-sector programs.
Ability to facilitate discussions with business users, technical teams, operations staff, agency representatives, and project leadership.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex operational or technical topics into clear, actionable documentation.
Experience supporting testing, validation, implementation readiness, change management, or operational transition activities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio or similar process-mapping tools.

Preferred Tolling and Transportation Experience

Experience with tolling, managed lanes, express lanes, open road tolling, all-electronic tolling, congestion pricing, or transportation technology projects.
Working knowledge of roadside tolling operations, including vehicle detection, transponder reads, license plate capture, classification, toll rules, trip building, and transaction processing.
Working knowledge of operational back-office and commercial back-office functions, including customer accounts, billing, payments, violations, image review, disputes, reconciliation, financial controls, and reporting.
Experience with MOMS, inventory control, asset management, maintenance workflows, or field operations support.
Experience developing or maintaining RTMs, configuration workbooks, business rules, SOPs, service blueprints, user stories, test plans, and acceptance criteria.
Familiarity with toll agency stakeholders, system integrators, customer service centers, payment processors, DMV or registration data exchanges, interoperability hubs, and enforcement processes.
Experience with Agile, hybrid delivery, or systems engineering environments supporting transportation technology implementation.

Salary Range

$135,000 to $155,000

Why Kimley-Horn?

At Kimley-Horn, we do things differently. People, clients, and employees are at the forefront of who we are. Clients know we prioritize achieving their goals and growing their success. Employees know our culture and approach to business are built on a desire to provide an environment for everyone to flourish. Our commitment to quality is only as good as the people behind it— that’s why we welcome and develop passionate, hardworking, and proactive employees. We take pride in how our employee retention, robust benefits package, and company values have led to Kimley-Horn’s placement on the Fortune “100 Best Companies to Work” list for 19 years!

Key Benefits at Kimley-Horn

Exceptional Retirement Plan: 2-to1- company match on up to 4% of eligible compensation (salary + bonus) and additional profit-sharing contribution.
Comprehensive Health Coverage: Low-cost medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
Time Off: Personal leave, flexible scheduling, floating holidays, and half-day Fridays.
Financial Wellness: Student loan matching in our 401(k), and performance-based bonuses.
Professional Development: Tuition reimbursement and extensive internal training programs.
Family-Friendly Benefits: New Parent Leave, family building benefits, and childcare resources.

This is an exciting opportunity for an early-career project professional to support the delivery of online sample and sample-driven market research projects. You will manage low-to-mid complexity projects from launch through completion while supporting senior team members on more complex engagements. The role combines project coordination, fieldwork management, client communication, data analysis, and operational quality control. You will work closely with Sales, Research Solutions, Operations, Programming, and external sample providers to keep projects on track. Your work will directly contribute to project quality, client satisfaction, timely delivery, and efficient use of resources. This role offers a fast-paced, collaborative environment where strong organization, analytical thinking, and attention to detail can make a measurable impact.

Accountabilities

Support the end-to-end execution of low-to-mid complexity online sample and sample-driven market research projects, ensuring deadlines and quality standards are consistently met.
Coordinate project launch activities, confirm fieldwork readiness, and monitor projects throughout the fielding process.
Track key field performance indicators, including incidence, completion rates, quotas, respondent flow, and project timelines.
Conduct data checks and quality assurance reviews during fieldwork and take action when performance or quality issues arise.
Manage fieldwork closeout activities, including reconciliations and honorarium-related processes.
Maintain proactive and professional communication with clients, providing project updates and escalating risks or issues when appropriate.
Collaborate with Sales, Research Solutions, Programming, Operations, and other internal stakeholders to align project scope, requirements, timelines, and deliverables.
Assist with sample planning and quota structures, including click-balancing and sampling adjustments during fieldwork.
Troubleshoot field performance challenges, recommend corrective actions, and coordinate with third-party sample vendors to optimize respondent flow and quality.
Support revenue tracking, forecasting, invoice preparation, and reconciliation activities for assigned projects.
Ensure scope changes are properly documented, communicated, and reflected in project records.
Maintain accurate project documentation, reporting, and debrief materials throughout the project lifecycle.
Contribute to process consistency, operational compliance, and continuous improvement within the Sample Solutions function.

Requirements

At least 2 years of relevant project coordination or project management experience, ideally within market research, online sampling, sample operations, or a related environment.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Understanding of market research fundamentals and primary research methodologies.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with clients, colleagues, and external partners.
Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities effectively in a fast-paced environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the ability to interpret field performance data and identify potential issues.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a distributed, cross-functional team.
Experience working with online panels or third-party sample providers is a plus.
Familiarity with CRM, project management, or project tracking systems is advantageous.
Experience managing quotas, click-balancing, or complex targeting criteria is preferred.
Experience creating project documentation, process guides, or training materials is an advantage.
Strong English-language communication skills and the ability to listen, analyze information, organize thoughts, and communicate concise, professional responses.
Comfortable working extensively with computers and digital collaboration tools.
Reliable, consistent, and responsive in communication with colleagues, stakeholders, and management.
Open to receiving and providing constructive feedback in a professional and positive manner.
Able to work in accordance with established policies, procedures, and professional standards.

Benefits

Full-time opportunity with a remote working arrangement in India.
Opportunity to work on diverse market research and consumer insights projects with measurable business impact.
Exposure to project management, sample operations, research methodologies, client engagement, and data-driven decision-making.
Collaboration with cross-functional teams including Sales, Research Solutions, Operations, Programming, and external partners.
Opportunity to develop expertise in online sampling, quota management, field performance, and project delivery.
Fast-paced environment offering opportunities to take ownership and develop professionally.
Career growth opportunities within a growing consumer insights and digital marketing environment.
Collaborative workplace culture centered on teamwork, respect, ownership, innovation, and continuous learning.
Opportunity to build project management and stakeholder management skills while working on increasingly complex engagements.

Join us in leading the
change!

At least 3 to 5 years managing utility-scale solar, BESS, wind, substation, or transmission projects.
Experience supporting projects through several of the following phases:
Development and due diligence
Design review
Procurement and RFP support
Construction oversight
Commissioning and performance testing
Substantial completion and project closeout
Experience managing multidisciplinary engineering reviews, including civil, structural, electrical, mechanical, SCADA, controls, substation, and interconnection.
Familiarity with EPC contracts, technical specifications, project schedules, payment applications, change orders, RFIs, submittals, NCRs, punch lists, and turnover documentation.
Experience coordinating site representatives, construction managers, inspectors, and testing personnel.
Prior consulting or client-facing experience strongly preferred.

Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned OE clients.
Develop and maintain project execution plans, deliverable registers, responsibility matrices, schedules, budgets, and action logs.
Coordinate internal engineering reviews and consolidate discipline comments into clear, client-ready deliverables.
Review project drawings, specifications, studies, calculations, equipment documentation, schedules, and contractor submittals.
Track technical risks, open items, design changes, construction issues, commissioning constraints, and contractual milestones.
Lead kickoff meetings, weekly project meetings, design-review calls, construction meetings, and monthly management reviews.
Manage full-time and periodic site personnel, including work priorities, reporting expectations, escalation paths, and deliverable quality.
Review field reports, photographs, punch lists, NCRs, test results, and commissioning records.
Support evaluation of payment applications, schedule updates, change orders, claims, and milestone completion.
Prepare concise written recommendations that clearly identify the issue, risk, required corrective action, responsible party, and due date.

Monitor project financial performance, staffing, utilization, scope compliance, and forecast-to-complete.
Identify out-of-scope requests and support preparation of amendments or additional-services proposals.
Escalate material safety, quality, schedule, cost, and technical risks promptly.
Support proposal development, staffing plans, fee estimates, client presentations, and business-development activities.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or a related technical field preferred.
Electrical, civil, mechanical, or structural engineering background is beneficial.
Professional Engineer license preferred but not required.
PMP, CCM, or similar project-management credential is beneficial.
OSHA 30 or equivalent construction-safety training preferred.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites required.

Travel Expectations

Approximately 20% to 40% travel, depending on project assignments.

. This position is a full-time opportunity located in Columbus, Ohio.

This role manages all aspects of medium-scale projects from initiation through completion, ensuring delivery on time, within budget, and in alignment with business objectives. As a Project Manager, Enterprise Culture & Programs, the selected individual will manage the full lifecycle of medium-scale projects while supporting enterprise-wide culture and program initiatives. Responsibilities may include:

ImmunityBio is a vertically integrated commercial stage biotechnology company developing next-generation therapies that bolster the natural immune system to defeat cancers and infectious diseases. The Opportunity

KWI keeps specialty retail running for Pandora, Bluemercury, Tom Ford, and dozens of other brands, and behind every storefront is an engineering team shipping constantly. Today those releases are coordinated on instinct and hallway conversations. You're here to change that. As our Technical Program Manager, you'll own the master release timeline, build the system that keeps every team aligned, and make shipping shorter, smoother, and more predictable, reporting straight to the CTO with a clear mandate to fix what slows us down.

The Company

We are a small team with a big vision: to be the premier provider of cloud technology solutions for retailers. KWI offers a unified commerce solution that is designed to help specialty retailers grow their business. Our portfolio of customers includes Pandora, Bluemercury, Tom Ford, and many other globally recognizable brands.

We combine Point of Sale, Merchandising, Order Management, eCommerce, CRM, and Loss Prevention into one cloud-based platform. We are a Values and Mission driven organization, and we believe that if we develop and demonstrate leadership in our strategy, operations, and people, we will continue to drive product innovation and service excellence.

As the Technical Program Manager, you excel at the following core competencies

Cross-team release coordination

Map and track cross-team dependencies; surface conflicts early and drive resolution before they become delays. Facilitate go/no-go checkpoints.

Process definition and documentation

Establish templates for cross-team planning: dependency maps, risk registers, status reports.

new_jobs.description:
Location:
Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type:
Direct Hire, Full-Time

Job Title:
Technical Project Manager

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

You will be our first dedicated project manager, and your job is to fix that. You own the work breakdown structure and the integrated schedule. You run the weekly coordination rhythm, record every task and decision so nothing is dropped, and stay ahead of the risks that quietly kill hardware schedules: long-lead parts, manpower shortages and skill gaps, missing equipment and infrastructure. Leadership will continue to set priorities, assign responsibility, and hold people accountable; your job is to make the plan legible and current so those decisions are made with real information, and so every person on the team knows what they need to be doing and when.

This is a role for someone who treats a well-built Gantt chart as a love language. Your best days end with the ambiguity banished from the plan and a name and a date on everything that matters. We are a startup: the process you bring must be the lightweight 20% that delivers 80% of the value, not a bureaucracy the team routes around.

Essential Duties

Schedule & WBS Ownership (Primary)

Build and own the work breakdown structure across our product lines: decompose engineering, manufacturing, test, and delivery work into tasks with owners, durations, dependencies, and dates
Build and maintain the integrated master schedule in a Gantt-based tool; keep it current enough that the team and leadership trust it as the single source of truth for what happens when
Identify and track the critical path; flag slips early and quantify their downstream impact so leadership can re-prioritize before a deadline is blown, not after
Translate customer commitments, demo dates, and test events into backward-planned schedules with explicit margin

Risk & Dependency Management

Maintain a living risk register for the things that actually derail hardware programs: long-lead and allocated parts, manpower shortages and skill gaps, missing equipment, tooling, and facility/infrastructure needs
Chase dependencies across engineering, purchasing, and the shop: surface the part that isn’t ordered, the fixture that isn’t built, and the test range that isn’t booked while there is still time to fix it
Work with the buyer on long-lead procurement timing so build schedules are planned around real lead times, and with leadership on staffing gaps before they become schedule slips

Coordination, Tasking & Communication

Run the weekly coordination meeting: set the agenda, drive it to decisions, and finish with every action item recorded with an owner and a due date
Be the recorder of tasking for the company: capture tasks and decisions from meetings, hallway conversations, and test events into one tracked system so nothing is missed or forgotten
Follow up on open actions between meetings; keep status honest without becoming the person the team hides from
Give leadership a clear, current picture of status, risks, and upcoming decisions that is short, factual, and free of surprises

Building the Structure

Stand up the company’s project management practices from scratch: task tracking, schedule reviews, action-item discipline, and deliverable definitions where none formally exist today
Select and administer the scheduling and task-tracking tools the company will run on, sized for a lean team: powerful enough to be trusted, light enough to be used
Establish just enough process to bring order to tasking and project planning without slowing a fast-iterating R&D team

Requirements

5+ years of project management experience on complex hardware / electromechanical development programs in robotics, defense, aerospace, automotive, industrial equipment, or similar
Technical background: an engineering degree or hands-on engineering experience on hardware products. You must be able to follow a technical discussion, ask credible questions, and earn the respect of a senior engineering team
Demonstrated ownership of a WBS and integrated schedule on a multi-disciplinary program: you built and ran the plan, not just reported on it
Expert fluency in Gantt-based scheduling tools (Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or similar): critical path, dependencies, baselines, and resource loading
Proven risk management on hardware programs, with a track record of catching long-lead, staffing, and equipment problems before they hit the schedule
Strong meeting facilitation and action-tracking discipline: you run tight meetings that end in owners and dates, and you close loops relentlessly
Comfortable leading through influence rather than authority: in this role, leadership sets priorities and holds people accountable; you make the plan visible, current, and impossible to ignore
Self-sufficient in a low-process environment: you impose structure on ambiguity rather than waiting for structure to be handed to you
US person (citizen or lawful permanent resident), required for ITAR compliance

Nice-to-Have

PMP, PMI-SP, or similar project management certification
Experience in a defense, ITAR-regulated, or government-customer environment, including milestone reviews, test events, and customer-driven schedules
Experience taking a hardware product from prototype through production transfer
Experience standing up project management practices at a startup or small company, rather than operating inside an established PMO
Working familiarity with manufacturing and machine-shop workflows, enough to plan realistically around fabrication, assembly, and test

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, a real WBS and integrated schedule exist and the team trusts them. The weekly coordination meeting runs on rails, every task has an owner and a date in one tracked system, and the first schedule-threatening risks (a long-lead part, a skills gap, a missing piece of equipment) have been caught and raised while they were still cheap to fix.
On an ongoing basis, nothing falls through the cracks. Everyone on the team can tell you what they need to be doing and when it is due. Leadership sets priorities against a schedule that reflects reality, slips are seen weeks out instead of discovered at the deadline, and the company hits its demo and delivery commitments because the plan was honest all along.

Work Environment

This role is based on-site in Austin, TX at our shop, working directly alongside the engineering and manufacturing team; the plan gets built by walking the floor, not from a remote dashboard. The environment is a working R&D and manufacturing facility for weapons systems: expect an active shop floor and proximity to live-fire test activity, with strict adherence to safety protocols. Occasional travel to test ranges and demonstration events to keep the schedule connected to what actually happens in the field.

Benefits

Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.
Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.
Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.
The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.
100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.
Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.
Zero Red Tape: You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.
Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.
Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

About The Interview

Initial screen with recruiter (30 min phone call)
Virtual interview with Director of HW Ops (45 min via MS Teams)
In-person interview (1 hour in Austin, TX) *9 Mothers will fly out candidates that are not local to the Austin area
Reference checks & offer

Compensation Range: $125K - $150K

new_jobs.description:

About Us

Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC, headquartered in Dallas, is a regulated electricity transmission and distribution business that uses superior asset management skills to provide reliable electricity delivery to consumers. Oncor (together with its subsidiaries) operates the largest transmission and distribution system in Texas, delivering power to nearly 4 million homes and businesses and operating more than 145,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in Texas.

Summary

The Regional Security Manager is responsible for executing Oncor’s Corporate Security (physical) program across a defined geographic region. This role ensures the protection of critical infrastructure, substations, field assets, and personnel through the application of enterprise security standards, risk-based controls, and operational discipline.

This position requires an autonomous professional who can translate enterprise security strategy into field execution in a geographically dispersed, high-risk critical infrastructure environment. The successful candidate will be required to be based out of West Texas and when not conducting field work, the primary reporting location for this position will be our office in Odessa.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Execute enterprise physical security strategy across the assigned region, ensuring alignment with corporate standards and risk tolerance for critical grid infrastructure.
Lead or co-lead regional physical security operations including:
Risk Assessments
Investigations
Incident Response
Site Surveys
Vendor Relationships
Law Enforcement Liaison
Conduct risk and vulnerability assessments across T&D infrastructure
Develop and implement layered security controls appropriate for utility environments, including remote and unmanned sites
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory and industry frameworks, including:
NERC CIP physical security requirements
Internal corporate security policies and standards
Lead regional incident response for physical security events, including:
Intrusions, vandalism, and theft
Sabotage or targeted attacks
Coordination with Enterprise Security & Resilience Center (ESRC)
Incident reporting and corrective actions

Monitor and assess regional threat environment and adjust posture accordingly
Oversee security technology deployment and operations, including:
Access control systems (ACS)
Video surveillance (CCTV, analytics)
Intrusion detection systems

Partner with engineering, operations, and capital projects teams to ensure security-by-design for:
New substations and infrastructure builds
Grid modernization projects
Hardening of existing assets
Manage and optimize third-party security vendors, including guard services, system integrators, and maintenance providers
Define and enforce SLAs and performance KPIs

Develop and maintain regional procedures, response protocols, and site-specific security plans
Build and maintain relationships with:
Local, state, and federal law enforcement
Fusion centers and intelligence-sharing groups

Lead regional security awareness efforts targeting field personnel, operators, and contractors
Develop, monitor, and report on regional metrics, including:
Security incidents at substations and facilities
Response times and law enforcement coordination
Technology health and effectiveness
Vendor performance

Provide regional input into executive-level reporting, including risk trends, mitigation progress, and emerging threats
Act as a change agent to elevate physical security maturity in a traditionally operational field environment
Build strong cross-functional partnerships
Perform all essential functions and other duties as assigned
Travel within Texas is required, approximately 50–60%, including frequent visits to remote field locations

Education & Experience

High school diploma, GED, or equivalent is required
Bachelor’s degree is encouraged to apply
7+ years in physical security, law enforcement, military, or critical infrastructure protection is required
5+ years managing multi-site or regional security operations is encouraged to apply
Experience responding to or managing incidents impacting operational resilience
Strong vendor management experience across guard force and electronic security systems providers

Skills

Deep understanding of physical security application in critical infrastructure environments
Ability to assess and prioritize risk across large geographic territories
Strong operational leadership in dynamic, field-based environments
Effective coordination with operations during high-impact events (storms, outages, attacks)
Strong communication and stakeholder influence skills across technical and non-technical groups
Analytical mindset with ability to translate incident data into actionable improvements
Experience with physical security systems in harsh or remote environments
Crisis leadership and decision-making under pressure
Strong organizational and execution discipline

Measures of Success

Effective implementation of layered security controls at critical sites
High performance and reliability of security technologies in field environments
Strong coordination with operations during incidents and storm response
Establish and maintain strong relationships with Law Enforcement partners
Demonstrated improvement in overall physical security maturity across the region

Physical Requirements

This role includes both office-based work and frequent field activity across a geographically dispersed region. The individual must be able to perform the essential job functions listed below:

Travel extensively (approximately 50–60%) within the assigned region, including driving long distances and accessing remote or rural locations. Focus of this will mainly be West TX
Conduct site visits and inspections at substations, field facilities, and other operational environments
Walk and stand for extended periods and navigate uneven terrain, including gravel, dirt, and undeveloped surfaces
Work outdoors in varying environmental conditions, which may include extreme heat, cold, wind, or precipitation
Lift, carry, push, and/or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds
Perform physical movements such as bending, stooping, kneeling, reaching, and climbing as necessary to complete site assessments and inspections

Maintain situational awareness and the ability to safely operate in active industrial and field environments.

Employee resource groups.

Competitive vacation, 10 company holidays and 2 personal holidays.

Salary continuation for up to 6 months for approved employee illness or injury.
Other perks such as commuter benefits, electric vehicle incentive program, appliance purchase plan.

The Physical Security Manager
is responsible for the operational management and execution of the credit union's physical security program. Reporting to the Director of Security, this position oversees daily security operations, Security Operations Center activities, security systems, and assigned personnel to help ensure the safety and security of associates, members, facilities, cash assets, and the organization's reputation.

The Physical Security Manager implements security strategies, policies, and procedures established by the Director of Security and serves as the primary operational leader for physical security activities across the organization. This position partners closely with departments including Fraud, Risk, Information Security, Human Resources, Facilities, and Operations to identify vulnerabilities, mitigate risks, and ensure effective security practices throughout the credit union.

Security Strategy, Governance & Program Leadership

Implement physical security policies, standards, procedures, and initiatives established by the Director of Security.
Manage day-to-day security operations and supervise assigned security personnel and Security Operations Center activities.
Monitor security program effectiveness and recommend operational improvements.
Support organization-wide security awareness and compliance efforts.
Provide operational guidance to managers and associates on physical security matters.
Act on behalf of the Director of Security when designated and provide leadership during their absence.

Physical Security Operations & Systems

Manage the daily operation of the Security Operations Center, including monitoring activities, incident response, and personnel coordination.
Oversee administration of access control systems, surveillance platforms, alarm systems, visitor management tools, and related technologies.
Coordinate equipment maintenance, testing, repairs, upgrades, and vendor support activities.
Monitor security operations across branch, ATM, and administrative locations to ensure compliance with established standards.
Conduct facility reviews and recommend security enhancements as needed.
Support implementation of physical security requirements for new facilities, remodels, relocations, and ATM deployments.

Risk Management, Assessments & Compliance

Conduct security assessments, inspections, and vulnerability reviews across credit union facilities.
Identify risks involving robbery, burglary, workplace violence, unauthorized access, fraud, and other security concerns.
Recommend corrective actions and assist with implementation of approved mitigation plans.
Support internal audits, examinations, and regulatory reviews related to physical security.
Maintain documentation supporting assessments, incidents, investigations, and compliance activities.
Partner with internal departments to address operational security concerns and emerging threats.

Incident Response & Investigations

Respond to and coordinate security incidents, threats, emergencies, and investigative activities.
Manage robbery response procedures, duress protocols, workplace violence response, and employee safety initiatives.
Coordinate with law enforcement agencies, emergency responders, and internal stakeholders during incidents.
Conduct investigations and gather evidence, documentation, video recordings, and other relevant information.
Perform post-incident reviews and implement approved corrective actions.
Escalate significant incidents and emerging threats to the Director of Security and other leadership as appropriate.

Security Awareness & Organizational Readiness

Deliver security training and awareness programs for associates and management.
Reinforce compliance with security policies, procedures, and operational standards.
Provide guidance regarding robbery response, suspicious activity, workplace violence prevention, and emergency procedures.
Support organizational preparedness through exercises, drills, and response planning activities.
Assist with development and maintenance of security procedures, reference materials, and training resources.

Vendor, Law Enforcement & Stakeholder Relationships

Maintain day-to-day working relationships with law enforcement agencies, monitoring providers, and security vendors.
Coordinate vendor service activities, maintenance schedules, and support requests.
Monitor vendor performance and communicate service concerns and improvement opportunities.
Collaborate with Fraud, Risk, Information Security, Human Resources, Facilities, and Operations teams to address security issues.
Maintain effective communication with associates and management regarding security-related activities and concerns.

Reporting, Analytics & Continuous Improvement

Prepare reports regarding incidents, investigations, assessments, inspections, and Security Operations Center activity.
Monitor trends and identify opportunities to improve security controls, processes, and operational effectiveness.
Track corrective actions and verify resolution of identified vulnerabilities.
Support preparation of management reports and presentations related to security risks and program performance.
Assist with implementation of security initiatives, technology enhancements, and continuous improvement efforts.
Perform other duties as assigned, ensuring accountability and alignment with organizational objectives.
Bachelor's degree in Criminal Justice, Security Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, or a related field preferred.
CPP, PSP, or another relevant security certification preferred or willingness to obtain.
5+ years of experience in physical security, corporate security, law enforcement, or a related field.
Prior supervisory or management experience preferred.
Experience conducting investigations, incident response, and security assessments.
Experience with access control, video surveillance, alarm systems, and security-related technologies.
Financial institution, banking, credit union, or other regulated industry experience preferred.
Strong operational leadership and organizational skills.
Knowledge of physical security principles, practices, and technologies.
Ability to identify risks and implement practical security solutions.
Strong investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Effective verbal, written, and training communication skills.
Ability to establish productive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.
Willingness to maintain a flexible schedule and respond to security-related priorities as needed.
