new_jobs.title: 【Ai Workforce】デプロイメントストラテジスト(Deployment Strategist) _金融
new_jobs.description:
事業概要

すべての経済活動のデジタル化を目指す株式会社LayerXは、Ai Workforce事業部において、「AIを業務に溶け込ませる」をコンセプトとした生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。
Ai Workforce事業部は2023年に発足した新規事業チームであり、幅広い業界のエンタープライズ企業パートナーとの取り組みを積み重ねてきました。大規模言語モデル（LLM）などのAIの技術は飛躍的に発展していますが、それ単体では本格的な業務で使うことが難しく、そのギャップを埋めるUX (AI-UX) を実現することを目指しています。
実証実験（PoC）ではなく、プロダクトとして既に続々とお客様にご導入いただいており、AIのポテンシャルを活かす更なるプロダクトの進化や、市場の拡大に取り組んでいます。

募集背景

Ai Workforce事業部では、日本を代表する大手企業を対象に、生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。
デプロイメントストラテジストは、エンジニアと協同してプロジェクトをリードし、プラットフォームが提供する「ナレッジ」「スキル」「ツール」「UI」という4種類のコンポーネントを自在に組み合わせ、顧客・業界単位で最適なAIエージェントを創り上げることをミッションとしています。
金融業界は、「膨大な非構造データ」と「厳密なルール」に基づく情報産業であり、膨大な書類の確認・審査等の人間がテキストを読んで判断・作成する業務が多く、LLM導入により劇的なコスト削減や収益向上が見込める領域です。
金融機関は「産業の血液」とも言われます。金融という心臓部をLLMにより強化することで、日本産業全体を力強く駆動します。

業務内容

プロジェクトマネジメント: 顧客の業務プロセスやAI活用方針を深く分析し、AIエージェント構築のプロジェクト設計を行います。
AIエージェント設計: エンジニア（Forward Deployed Engineer）とペアを組み、Ai Workforceの4つのコンポーネント（ナレッジ、スキル、ツール、UI）を組み合わせ、顧客・業界単位で最適化されたAIエージェントを設計・構築します。
プロダクトマネジメント: 上記4つのコンポーネント自体の機能追加やバージョンアップに関するプロダクトマネジメントを担当します。
新規ソリューションの立ち上げ: 個々の案件で得られた知見を体系化し、業界・職務単位で汎用的な「ソリューション」として企画・開発します。

ポジションの魅力

コンサルタントとしての強みを土台に、自分自身の手で事業やプロダクトを作る経験やキャリアを構築できます。
エンジニア（Forward Deployed Engineer）と密接に協働し、AIの先端技術が大企業や社会に実装していく過程に深く関与できます。
国内有数の金融機関が競争優位性を構築する過程を自ら企画・実装し、変革の姿を目の当たりにすることができます。

必要な条件/経験

コンサルティングファームまたはそれに類する企業での勤務経験（3年以上）
エンジニアを巻き込み、大企業のプロジェクトマネジメントを行った経験
金融機関向けの提案・デリバリー経験
上記に加えて下記いずれかの経験
エンジニア経験
AIやデータサイエンスのプロジェクト経験
戦略コンサルタントとしての経験
日本語にてコミュニケーションが可能なこと / Native level－like fluency in Japanese

望ましい経験/スキル

プロダクトの企画やデザインに携わった経験（ユーザー視点で必要な機能・体験を考え、開発ロードマップに反映させたこと）
マネージャー以上の職位の経験
営業活動の経験

こんな方と働きたい

LayerXのミッション「すべての経済活動を、デジタル化する。」に共感する方
行動指針「徳 , Trustful Team , Bet AI , Fact Base ,Be Animal」に共感する方

new_jobs.description:
About Giga

Giga is building gigawatts of AI data centers to hasten a future of intelligence and abundance. We build data centers fast and at scale by combining the capabilities of an equipment supplier, engineering firm, general contractor, and real estate developer under one roof. Our team moves quickly and thinks practically. If you're ready to make an impact in an industry that matters, we're looking for people like you.

Why join Giga

The Pace: We're building at a speed most companies talk about but never actually operate at. If you've been bored somewhere else, you won't be here.
The Impact: Every person at Giga touches the work that matters. No layers, no waiting for approval chains. You'll see your fingerprints on what we ship.
The Team: A team of operators defining the future of AI infrastructure. We recruit A-players from the most innovative companies in the world, and they choose Giga because the work here means more.
The Moment: AI doesn't run without power, and that's us. Giga is the picks and shovels behind the AI revolution. This industry is about to explode, and you'll be in the room where it's already happening.

What You’ll Do

As the EHS & S Manager,
you will own the full Environmental, Health, Safety & Security (EHS&S) function at our Houston manufacturing facility — from OSHA and environmental regulatory compliance to hazard-specific programs covering high-voltage electrical testing, transformer oil/dielectric fluid handling, overhead crane operations, and hot work. You'll also serve as the site lead for physical security, access control, and emergency preparedness. You'll work closely with plant leadership, production supervisors, and corporate HSE to build a proactive safety culture and keep the facility fully compliant with federal, state, and local requirements.

Where you’ll work

We are an in-office culture — velocity matters when you're building physical infrastructure, and the best decisions happen in the room. This role is based full-time on-site at our Houston, TX manufacturing facility, with regular presence on the production floor, testing areas, and warehouse/yard.

Responsibilities

Environmental, Health & Safety Program Leadership

Develop, implement, and maintain the facility's written HSE programs in compliance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910 (General Industry) and applicable EPA/TCEQ environmental regulations
Own facility-specific safety programs including electrical safety/arc flash (NFPA 70E) for 480V system testing, lockout/tagout, overhead crane and rigging safety, hot work, and PPE
Manage safe handling, storage, and spill response procedures for mineral oil-based transformer dielectric fluid and other regulated fluids used in production and testing
Lead job hazard analyses (JHAs) for manufacturing, testing, and maintenance operations, and ensure controls are implemented and followed
Conduct regular facility safety inspections and audits; track findings to closure and drive continuous improvement in safety performance
Investigate incidents, near-misses, and injuries; determine root cause and implement corrective/preventive actions
Maintain OSHA recordkeeping (300/300A/301 logs) and ensure timely, accurate incident reporting to OSHA and internal stakeholders
Manage the facility's industrial hygiene program, including noise, air quality, and exposure monitoring where applicable

Environmental Compliance

Maintain compliance with applicable air, water, waste, and chemical storage regulations (e.g., SPCC, hazardous waste generator requirements, stormwater permits)
Manage environmental permits, inspections, and regulatory reporting for the Houston facility
Oversee proper handling, storage, and disposal of used transformer oil, solvents, and other regulated waste streams

Training & Culture

Develop and deliver HSE training, including HAZCOM, electrical safety, LOTO, crane/rigging, confined space (as applicable), PPE, and emergency response
Partner with plant leadership and supervisors to build a strong site-wide safety culture and hold teams accountable to HSE standards
Maintain training records and certifications for all employees and relevant contractors

Security

Manage physical security for the facility, including access control systems, badge/visitor management, and security camera systems
Develop and maintain site security procedures, including protocols for after-hours access, contractor/vendor access, and asset protection
Serve as the facility's primary point of contact for security incidents, and coordinate with local law enforcement as needed
Conduct periodic security risk assessments and recommend improvements to physical security controls

Emergency Preparedness

Develop and maintain the facility's Emergency Action Plan, including evacuation procedures, severe weather (hurricane) response, and medical emergency response
Coordinate emergency drills and ensure employees are trained on emergency procedures
Maintain relationships with local fire, EMS, and emergency management agencies

Reporting & Leadership

Report on EHS&S performance metrics, incident trends, and program status to plant and corporate leadership
Manage the EHS&S budget for the facility, including PPE, training, equipment, and contracted services
Serve as the facility's primary point of contact for OSHA, environmental agencies, and other regulatory bodies during inspections or audits

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of progressive EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment, including at least 2 years in a leadership/managerial role
Strong working knowledge of OSHA 1910 General Industry standards, including electrical safety, LOTO, and crane/material handling requirements
Experience managing environmental compliance programs in a manufacturing setting
Experience developing and leading physical security programs, or a demonstrated ability to take on this responsibility
Strong incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and corrective action skills
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence and hold cross-functional teams accountable to safety standards

Bonus points

Experience with electrical equipment manufacturing, testing, or transformer/dielectric fluid handling
Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), or similar certification
OSHA 30-Hour General Industry certification; NFPA 70E qualified electrical worker training
Experience with security system administration (access control, CCTV) or prior security management background

How We Work

We value people who take ownership, raise risks early, communicate directly, and follow through. Incomplete information is part of the job. Make the best decision you can, document it, and adjust as the facts change. Move quickly on reversible decisions and take more care when security, safety, financial, employee, or customer risk is involved.

Benefits

Subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance
Equity (options) in a rapidly growing startup
401(k) with 4% employer match
Unlimited PTO
Parental leave
Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) or Health Savings Account (HSA)
Commuter benefits, where applicable
Opportunities to collaborate in person at periodic team and company on-sites

We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Giga Energy complies with all applicable labor laws, including the California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and other relevant state and federal regulations. We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

The Environmental Business Line of AECOM is seeking a Hazardous Building Material/Industrial Hygiene Project Manager for immediate employment with the Northeast department of the EHS & Air Practice. This candidate is expected to report to the Boston, MA, Chelmsford, MA, or Manchester, NH office.

The appropriately qualified applicant will be able to demonstrate at least 8 years of experience performing and managing building hazardous material (asbestos, lead paint, etc.) surveys, abatement oversight, and design and/or industrial hygiene projects. This is anticipated to be a seller/doer role, combining technical project execution with business development. On the business development side, responsibilities will include identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, developing client relationships, and securing contracts (both internally and externally). This dual role requires a balance of technical expertise, project management skills, and business acumen to successfully grow the business while delivering exceptional service to clients.

The job responsibilities for this position will include but are not limited to:
Managing and/or self-performing a wide range of hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects for both private and public-sector clients
Collaborating with other licensed/certified professionals and technical/regulatory specialists on hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects. These projects are expected to include survey and investigation work, abatement/remediation design, and abatement/remediation.
Provide technical and/or regulatory leadership for hazardous building material and industrial hygiene projects throughout New England, the US, and internationally.
Develop proposals, including work scope, budgets and schedules for hazardous building material survey/design/abatement and other industrial hygiene projects.
Manage or provide review of technical work and field activities, including performing oversight of projects to confirm work is being done in accordance with the contracted scope of work, budget, schedule and regulatory/industry standards.
Review, coordinate or prepare written reports, work plans, and technical memorandum; analyze data and develop supported conclusions.
Work collaboratively with other teams within the EHS department, Environment business line, and across AECOM’s other internal business lines.
Proactively identify opportunities to increase project efficiencies and add value to client service offerings.
Identifying and pursuing new business opportunities and supporting department growth through supporting internal and external sales.

The successful candidate will have enough technical experience to be able to independently manage various sized field efforts and deliver associated reports for a wide variety of hazardous building material projects/surveys and industrial hygiene projects. They should possess strong interpersonal and communication abilities to effectively engage with team members, clients, and stakeholders. This candidate will be committed to the team’s success and growth; will rigorously apply safety policies and procedures; and will effectively manage the quality of field efforts and project deliverables within the bounds of AECOM’s Quality Management System. This position calls for excellent organization and time management skills, flexibility to work on a multitude of diverse projects, a positive attitude, and a willingness to support the mentorship and growth of staff.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

BA/BS + 8 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and or education.
Technical experience directly related to building hazardous material (asbestos, lead paint, etc.)
Industrial hygiene, mold, or indoor air quality experience.
Must have 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training.
Must have EPA AHERA Asbestos Inspector Certification.
Must have New England State specific licenses and certifications pertaining to asbestos (MA, ME, NH, CT) or be eligible to obtain such licenses and certifications.
Valid Driver’s License and must be able to pass AECOM’s Motor Vehicle Records review.
Due to the nature of work US Citizenship is required

Preferred Qualifications:

One or more of the following certifications: EPA Asbestos Management Planner, EPA Asbestos Project Designer, EPA Asbestos Supervisor, EPA Lead Risk Assessor.
New England State Asbestos Designer licenses (MA, CT, ME)
Experience with strategy and growth plan development and execution
Certified Industrial Hygienist
Certified Safety Professional
Experience in developing scope, fee, and terms for proposals for interdisciplinary teams related to hazardous material services
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities
Ability to interact with architects and engineers on fast-paced building renovation designs requiring the development of asbestos/building hazardous materials program requirements, drawings, specifications, and design narratives.
Experience managing and/or mentoring a team of technical professionals
Experience managing small to large size public and private sector projects
Experience managing scope and budget, and staff administration and development
Experience building client relationships, business development and client management
Highly effective verbal and written communication skills; extremely proficient in technical writing; highly effective organization and multi-tasking skills.
Internally driven, self-starter, team oriented

Additional Information

Relocation is not available for this position
Sponsorship is not available for this position
Willing to travel out-of-town for durations ranging from approximately one week to three months, as needed. Travel will vary greatly and depend on the workload/projects at any given time.

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. About the Company
Persistent Systems is a leading global technology company dedicated to delivering innovative software solutions and digital transformation services. With a strong focus on healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and other critical industries, Persistent Systems leverages cutting-edge technologies to help organizations optimize their operations, improve patient outcomes, and achieve strategic goals. The company prides itself on fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and dynamic work environment that nurtures talent and promotes continuous learning. With a commitment to excellence and integrity, Persistent Systems has established a reputation for delivering high-quality solutions tailored to client needs across the globe.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Data Analyst specializing in healthcare data to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will possess strong expertise in MS SQL, healthcare data modeling, data integration, and statistical analysis. In this role, you will play a key part in building scalable cloud infrastructure, implementing system health monitoring, and developing continuous integration pipelines. Your insights will support critical healthcare initiatives such as value-based care, population health, and operational efficiency. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze large healthcare datasets, create comprehensive reports, and develop data workflows that drive strategic decision-making. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work with state-of-the-art technologies in a fast-paced, innovative environment, contributing to impactful healthcare projects.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Healthcare Analytics, or a related field. A minimum of 7 years of hands-on experience working with US healthcare datasets, including claims, benefits, and eligibility data, is essential. Proficiency in SQL for querying and analyzing complex healthcare data is required, along with familiarity with modern data warehousing platforms such as Snowflake and MySQL. Experience in creating healthcare process flows and data documentation using tools like Microsoft Visio or draw.io is highly desirable. Candidates should demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to validate and transform data accurately. Excellent communication skills are necessary to effectively collaborate with technical teams and non-technical stakeholders, translating complex data insights into clear, actionable reports.

Responsibilities
As a Data Analyst in Healthcare at Persistent Systems, your responsibilities will include analyzing large-scale healthcare datasets, including claims, provider, utilization, and quality metrics. You will write and optimize complex SQL queries to extract, validate, and analyze healthcare data from relational databases, ensuring data accuracy and integrity. Supporting data validation, reconciliation, and transformation processes will be vital to meet business and regulatory reporting requirements. You will work closely with data engineering teams to support the ingestion and integration of data from various source systems such as claims processing platforms, provider databases, and eligibility feeds. Developing and maintaining healthcare data models, marts, and analytics layers on platforms like Snowflake and MySQL will be a core part of your role. You will also create process maps, data lineage diagrams, and system architecture visuals to document healthcare workflows, business rules, and metrics definitions. Collaborating with stakeholders across healthcare operations, finance, clinical, quality, and compliance teams, you will translate complex healthcare data into clear insights, presenting findings and recommendations to leadership and cross-functional teams. Additionally, you will support analytics initiatives aimed at improving healthcare quality, operational efficiency, and population health outcomes.

Benefits
Persistent Systems offers a competitive salary package complemented by comprehensive benefits designed to support our employees' well-being and professional growth. Our culture emphasizes talent development, providing quarterly growth opportunities, and sponsoring higher education and certification programs. Employees benefit from working with cutting-edge technologies and engaging in innovative projects. We foster a vibrant work environment with engagement initiatives such as team-building events, flexible work hours, and recognition programs like Long Service awards. Annual health check-ups and insurance coverage—including group term life, personal accident, and Mediclaim hospitalization for employees and their families—are provided to ensure health and security. Our commitment to work-life balance and continuous development makes Persistent Systems an ideal place for ambitious professionals to thrive and advance their careers.

Equal Opportunity (in last)
Persistent Systems is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, regardless of gender, gender identity, or ethnicity. We support hybrid work arrangements and flexible hours to accommodate diverse lifestyles. Our facilities are accessible and equipped with ergonomic setups and assistive technologies to support employees with physical disabilities. If you have specific requirements, please inform us during the application process or at any point during your employment. We believe that diversity and inclusion drive innovation and excellence, and we are dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can succeed.

Safety and Security Manager- 48th Ave

OUR PURPOSE

Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Denver has been serving Northern Colorado since 1927. We serve tens of thousands of people each year in seven ministries: Marisol Services, Early Childhood Education, Shelter Services, Catholic Charities Housing, St. Raphael Counseling, Family, Kinship, and Senior Services; and Parish & Community Engagement.

Purpose Of Position

A Safety and Security Manager at Catholic Charities:

Maintains and oversees the safety & security team schedule; schedules safety & security associates and supervisors to work shifts and locations. Oversees safety & security coverage at all locations.
Integrates the leadership model in daily activities, including spot coaching, supervision, and training.
Assists the Director in tracking team compliance with all training and certifications.
Approves safety & security team timecards, PAL/EIB requests, and conducts employee evaluations and supervisions.
Ensures that all safety & security associates and supervisors have completed all reports, incident reports (IRs), Apricot entries, and other documentation in a timely and professional manner.
Serves as a member of the Safety Team and is trained on the Emergency Operations Plan.
Politely welcomes, greets, and assists all participants and visitors, providing routine information or directing them to the appropriate staff/programs.
Monitors surveillance cameras and public areas to ensure no improper conduct or unauthorized persons are inside the facility and/or on agency property.
Adheres to Agency confidentiality and HIPAA expectations.
Responds and assists as appropriate with any emergencies in the building or on the grounds.
Maintains current knowledge of ongoing events and changes by reading reports, entries, and databases.
Maintains shelter rules and standards uniformly and consistently.
Responds appropriately to needs and crises, such as mediating basic interpersonal problems between participants and summoning emergency personnel.
Communicates with other staff to resolve problems with individual participants.
Keeps the Director informed of shelter developments.
Models Catholic Charities’ commitment to treating all persons with respect and dignity.
On call for consultation and intervention after hours and on weekends.
Regular and predictable attendance.
Completes security guard training and licensing.
Completes all mandatory training as stated by the agency or supervisor.
Supports implementation and oversight of security technology, including access control, alarms, and surveillance systems.
Collaborates with police departments on CPTED (Crime Prevention through Environmental Design) reports or similar assessments to be completed at least once every 2 years and leads to the implementation of changes.
Serves as a point of contact for law enforcement, emergency responders, and security vendors as needed.
Coordinates emergency drills and preparedness activities with the Director for internal teams and external partners.
May be required to travel to other sites for emergencies, training, or business need.
Employees may be required to work at or provide temporary coverage at other shelter locations based on operational and business needs.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Manager will supervise Catholic Charities’ Safety and Security Associates and Supervisors for the Shelters Team at 48th Avenue, Smith Road, and Holy Rosary. The Manager may also be asked to provide support at Samaritan House in Downtown Denver.

Managers may provide guidance and direction to members of other teams, including operations, facilities, etc.

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS

Demonstrated experience in employee supervision.
Experience/knowledge in security management, de-escalation, crisis management, and safety preferred.
Ability to work effectively within the framework of Catholic teachings.
Strong organizational, communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
Ability to effectively lead and motivate staff through the application of Agency values.
Intermediate knowledge of computers to input data, create and generate reports, and maintain communications.
Knowledge of the service population’s cultural and socioeconomic characteristics and the appropriate techniques and practices for the client population.
Ability to interact effectively as a team member and independently with Agency staff and with a diverse client base.

EDUCATION And/or EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) from an accredited four-year college or university in a related field preferred; and three to five years of related safety or security experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Security Guard license if in the City/County of Denver. Must be obtained within 30 days of employment.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary:
$60,000 - $70,000 per year. Full-time.

Training:
We provide a robust training curriculum that will support our employees throughout their career. Training provided within the first year of employment includes: De-escalation & Safety; Mental Health First Aid; Substance Abuse & Mental Health; Human Trafficking; Trauma-Informed Care; and many more.

Benefits:
In addition to being part of a higher purpose while working in a challenging yet rewarding environment, eligible Catholic Charities employees receive a generous benefits package, including:

The shift is full-time, with the possibility of remote/hybrid work one day per week.
Extensive Paid Time Off (4 weeks accrual for new employees - increasing based on tenure), promoting work-life balance.
15 Paid holidays annually (shelters are 24/7, so if a holiday is worked, holiday pay is included)
Sabbatical Leave Program: Employees who have completed seven years of continuous full-time service are eligible for paid sabbatical leave to support rest, renewal, and professional or personal growth. Eligible staff may take 4 weeks of sabbatical leave.
403b Retirement Plan with Agency contribution of 4% & match up to 2% of annual compensation.
Choice of 3 PPO Medical Plans (90% of employee's and 75% of dependent’s premiums are paid by Agency), Dental & Vision starting the 1st day of the month following their start date.
May be eligible for Public Service Loan Forgiveness through Federal Student Loans and many more benefits.

ARE YOU READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

We look forward to meeting you!

We conduct background checks as part of our hiring process.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

KMEA (KMEA.com) is an organization owned by ninety Kansas municipalities that empowers its members to excel as high-quality electric utilities. With KMEA’s help in the areas of advocacy, power supply, energy market participation, regulatory representation, etc., member cities ensure that reliable and affordable electricity is available to their citizens. To fulfill our mission, team members must value integrity, respect, the needs of our member communities, safety, and teamwork.

Position Description

Position Title:               Operations Analyst
Department:                Electric Operations
Reports to:                     Director, Resource Planning & Development
FLSA Status:                Non-Exempt

The position supports electric operations and monthly billing functions.  The role emphasizes strong analytical and creative problem-solving skills, proficiency in database management, and familiarity with electric‑utility data and billing concepts. We are a small organization, so responsibilities will be diverse. The position can be upgraded to Senior Operations Analyst depending on qualifications and experience.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

·       Maintain and enhance database systems and files used for operational reporting and billing
·       Build tools and queries that streamline billing and operations processes
·       Collect, clean, and validate large datasets (ETL) from systems such as metering, billing, and asset management platforms
·       Support back‑office teams by validating third-party invoices, analyzing exceptions, reconciling discrepancies, performing cost allocation calculations, and creating and issuing monthly invoices
·       Document processes and dbase structures for internal reference and training
·       Learn and become proficient in energy market activities such as congestion hedging and renewable energy certificate management

Required Qualifications

·       Effective problem‑solving, communication, and documentation skills
·       Prior experience as a data analyst or database administrator
·       Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, complex formulas)
·        Proficiency in Microsoft Access and SQL Server or similar database platforms, including design, queries, forms, and reports.
·        Associate’s degree or higher

Preferred Qualifications

·       Bachelor of science degree (or higher) in computer science, finance, or related fields
·       Efficient prompt engineering ability with AI tools
·       Knowledge of the electric utility sector and Southwest Power Pool or similar energy markets
·       Experience with basic coding, APIs, Power BI, and UI (Utilities Intl.) or similar
·       Experience with basic accounting and invoicing concepts

Candidate Characteristics

·       Aptitude and creativity for process improvement and problem solving
·       Ability to translate complex data into clear insights for non‑technical stakeholders
·       Capacity to prioritize workflow and perform effectively with competing responsibilities without supervision and within established deadlines
·       Can interact effectively and professionally with others and provide exceptional service, both internally and externally

Work Environment and Demands

·       On-site Monday-Friday along with our full-time staff of fifteen in our stand-alone office in highly acclaimed Overland Park, Kansas
·       Limited travel; mostly day trips within Kansas (e.g., city meetings, conferences), sometimes with short notice
·       Business casual attire, limited physical demands, typical office environment, including most hours spent at a computer
·       This position has no supervisory responsibilities

new_jobs.description:
At ENFRA, we blend a rich history with a forward-looking vision. With over 100 years of experience, we are a pillar of stability in the energy infrastructure industry and a leader in innovative energy solutions. Our commitment to leveraging emerging technologies ensures that we remain at the forefront of the Energy-as-a-Service sector.

We believe in growth—not just for our business, but for our people. Our team members have the opportunity to advance their careers in a supportive environment that values continuous learning and development. We embrace innovation and encourage creative problem solving to tackle the energy infrastructure and energy challenges of tomorrow.

Inclusion is at the heart of our culture. We strive to create a workplace where every voice is heard and valued, fostering a collaborative environment where diverse perspectives drive our success.

Join us to be part of a legacy of excellence and a future of groundbreaking advancements. At ENFRA, stability, innovation, and growth are more than just values—they are the pillars of our continued success.

Overview

The Pre-Construction Business Analyst serves as a strategic and operational partner to the Director of IS Pre-Construction. This role is responsible for transforming data into actionable insights, developing executive-ready communications, supporting decision-making processes, and driving organizational efficiency. The position provides analytical, reporting, research, presentation, and administrative support while helping improve execution readiness, risk visibility, resource planning, and business performance across the Energy-as-a-Service portfolio.

Responsibilities

Build professional PowerPoint presentations for executive reviews, opportunity reviews, client presentations, and project governance meetings
Conduct research on industry trends, competitors, healthcare and higher education markets, client profiles, and emerging EaaS opportunities.
Collect, validate, and analyze project, financial, resource, and operational data to identify risks, trends, and improvement opportunities.
Maintain pipeline tracking tools and assist in evaluating project readiness, workload forecasts, and resource demand.
Develop SOPs, workflows, process maps, templates, and best practices that improve consistency, scalability, and operational efficiency.
Maintain accountability trackers, decision registers, risk logs, and leadership action plans to ensure timely execution of commitments.
Manage project information from internal and external stakeholders; and distribute to project team.
Continuously track project metrics to ensure that the project is delivered on time, and on budget.
Manage schedule and time to acquire a knowledge of all aspects of pricing for projects including constructability narratives, direct contractor pricing, financial pricing model, definitive transaction documents, etc.
Uphold the Company owner advocacy philosophy and organizational core values.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Education, Experience, and Qualifications

Four Year college degree. Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering from a four year ABET accredited university or related technical or construction management degree.
0-2 Years experience
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills and aptitude.
Ability to communicate effectively verbally and in written format
Ability to communicate effectively with facility managers and engineers.
Ability to work independently to meet deadlines
Ability to manage time effectively to meet project deadlines.
Ability to use technology and apps for collecting data
Passion for quality and client satisfaction
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Detail oriented and willing to tackle various ongoing projects in a fast paced environment.
Well versed in the industry and the Company's competitors.
Excellent multitasking skills, with the ability to perform duties outside of scope of work when necessary

Preferred experience with building energy services in the health and higher-education field.
Experience with financial plans and budget objectives.
Knowledge of the comprehensive business model and energy market dynamics.
Knowledge of the energy industry and related law, systems, codes and economics

new_jobs.description:
Responsibilities

Position Summary:

As a Business Data Analyst, you will play a key role in analyzing and interpreting data from multiple sources, leverage data driven insights and automation solutions to guide strategic business decisions, streamline data workflows, and improve operational efficiency. This role requires strong technical skills, with a focus on data automation and process optimization. The ideal candidate possesses a strong analytical mindset and a strong problem-solving abilities, and can translate complex datasets into scalable, automated solutions and actionable business recommendations.

Position Responsibilities May Include, But Not Limited To

Data Automation, Analysis & Interpretation

Extract, clean, and analyze large datasets from multiple data sources (JDE, KOMPASS, MBSYNC, Samsara, Paragon, among others) and data warehouse (Snowflake) to enable automated insights into business performance
Design and maintain automated workflows and data pipelines to reduce manual reporting and improve data accuracy. Conduct deep-dive analyses to identify patterns, trends, and relationships that inform business decisions
Assist in the design and deployment of analytics analysis to support process optimization and data insights
Perform root cause analysis of business challenges and recommend automated, data-driven solutions
Identify opportunities for process improvements, cost reductions, and efficiency gains using data and automation
Ensure data quality and accuracy through proper validation techniques, best practices and governance processes

Reporting and Visualization

Design, develop, and maintain automated reports, dashboards, and visualizations
Collaborate with department heads to define and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) relevant to the company’s strategic goals
Translate business questions into data requirements and provide concise answers through self-service reporting and automation

Alternative Solutions (Machine Learning and AI Integration)

Work with the global team to identify opportunities for alternative solutions
Assist and support in the deployment of models that support operational decision-making
Evaluate results and continuously improve automated solutions to align with business objectives
Stay updated on emerging technologies and integrate modern automation techniques into business workflows

Data Quality & Governance

Maintain data integrity, ensure consistency across automated processes. Collaborate with data ingestion and IT teams to close data gaps and improve automation readiness
Ensure compliance with data privacy and internal governance standards
Ensure data quality and accuracy through proper validation techniques, best practices and governance processes

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work closely with various business units (Operations & Transportation, Finance, Supply Chain, ROP, REX, Centralized Routing) to understand their business needs and develop tailored automation or reporting solutions. Present automated data insights and recommendations to senior leadership
Serve as a liaison between technical teams (data ingestion, engineering) and business stakeholders to align automation efforts with priorities

Project Management

Lead or contribute to cross-functional projects focused on
data automation, insight generation, and continuous improvement. Track project milestones and ensure timely delivery of automation initiatives
Other projects or duties as assigned

Qualifications

Required Skills and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science or a related field. 2-4+ years of experience data automation and process optimization. Experience building Extract, Transform & Load (ETL) processes and managing data pipelines across multiple data sources and warehouses
Willingness to understand business operations and identify automation opportunities
Experience of scripting languages (like Python, R, SQL) and data process workflow automation tools
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy
Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex data topics to non-technical stakeholders. Eagerness to explore alternative solutions that support data automation and process optimization insight delivery
Collaborative mindset with a passion for innovation and continuous improvement
This position must pass a post-offer background check

Master’s degree preferred

new_jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Credit Risk
new_jobs.description:
Experience in credit risk analytics, ECL and loss forecasting experience, alongside SQL skills and the confidence to influence senior stakeholders
Own and shape Zip’s ECL and loss forecasting processes, turning complex credit risk data into insights that influence important business decisions
Work flexibly in a hybrid role from our Sydney or Melbourne office

Write your story with a career at Zip

With a broad remit across credit risk strategy and decisioning, forecasting, portfolio analytics and controls monitoring, our Risk Management & Data Science team is a key strategic interface between the business and a varied range of internal and external stakeholders.

Working with world class platforms and given the freedom to experiment and uplift your analytical and modelling capabilities, you’ll be a part of a flat structure and a close knit team responsible for improving the commercials related to arrears and repayments.

As a Senior Data Analyst in Credit Risk Management, you’ll take end to end ownership of Zip’s Expected Credit Loss and loss forecasting processes. You’ll connect portfolio performance with ECL, losses and forward looking forecasts, while continually improving the quality, automation and explainability of our approach.

This is an opportunity to combine deep analytical thinking with meaningful stakeholder influence, partnering closely with Credit Risk, Finance and Data to turn complex movements into clear insights and recommendations.

What You’ll Own

Own the monthly ECL operating cycle and loss forecasting process, delivering accurate, timely and explainable outcomes
Lead quarterly ECL parameter monitoring, investigating material movements and connecting changes in portfolio performance with expected loss outcomes
Continuously improve the ECL production code base, automation, controls, repeatability and turnaround times
Strengthen data governance and controls, identifying data quality issues early and partnering with our Data team to resolve them
Lead regular ECL discussions with senior Credit Risk and Finance stakeholders, translating complex analysis into clear insights, decisions and actions
Own the methodology, assumptions, scenario analysis and variance analysis underpinning loss forecasts, continually looking for opportunities to improve forecast accuracy
Lead the annual ECL review, including methodology and performance assessments, back testing, documentation and support for internal and external audit activity
Explore how AI and new technology can make our forecasting and analytical processes faster, smarter and more effective
Provide analytical support for bad debt sale initiatives and other emerging Credit Risk priorities

What You'll Bring To The Team

Zipsters work on a broad range of initiatives, and our skills and experiences all look a little different. What really matters to us is that you’re a great fit with our four Values, and have a desire to learn and grow.

So whether you meet some or all of the desirable attributes below, we’d still love to hear from you:

Experience in credit risk analytics within retail banking, consumer finance or another regulated financial services environment
Strong experience in credit loss forecasting or portfolio loss analytics, with the ability to connect portfolio performance, delinquency and write offs with expected loss outcomes
Practical experience with ECL, including PD, LGD and EAD, impairment processes and credit risk parameter monitoring
Strong SQL skills and experience maintaining analytical code, with exposure to Python, R or SAS highly regarded
A disciplined approach to data quality, testing, controls, documentation and production change management
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the confidence to explain analytical outcomes, challenge assumptions and lead discussions with senior stakeholders
The ability to translate complex analysis into clear recommendations that support effective decision making
A mindset that embraces AI and new tools to adapt, learn and grow.
An aptitude for identifying and managing risks. Whether you are a People Manager or an Individual Contributor, we are all leaders at Zip, therefore effective risk management is important to how we run our business and part of all our roles.
Our values in your DNA: Customer First, Own It, Stronger Together and Change the Game

What You’ll Get In Return

As we write this next exciting chapter in our story, we will continue to move at pace and embrace change. For you, this might mean opportunities to learn new skills with hands-on experience, broader responsibilities, or the buzz of seeing your work impact customers faster.

Zip is a place where you’ll get out exactly what you put in. When you join the team, we'll do our best to make sure you can be yourself and surround yourself with smart, friendly colleagues and leaders who have your back, so that you can make the big things happen.

Zipsters tell us these are just some of the best things about working here. You’ll also receive:

25 days paid leave annually, including birthday leave and quarterly wellbeing days
16 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers, and 4 weeks for supporting carers
Family support policies including miscarriage bereavement leave and domestic violence leave
Mental health and wellness initiatives, including $299 annual wellbeing allowance, free access for you and family members to our EAP service Sonder, discounted private health insurance, and great rates on fitness sessions through ClassPass
2 days paid volunteering leave per year
Access to the Flare Benefits Hub and Novated Leasing for savings across lifestyle, essentials and wellbeing
Fee-free Zip products, and discounts with Zip merchant partners
Team social events, epic offices, free breakfast daily, and weekly free lunches

Be a part of a team that reflects the diversity of our customers

We pride ourselves on being a workplace that provides equal opportunities to people of all ages, cultural backgrounds, sexual orientations, gender identities, abilities, veteran status, and everything else that makes you unique.

Equally, we’re committed to ensuring our recruitment processes are accessible and inclusive. Please let us know If there are any adjustments that need to be made to ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

And finally…get to know us

Zip Co Limited (ASX: ZIP) is a digital financial services company, offering innovative, people-centred products that bring customers and merchants together.

Operating in two core markets - Australia and the US, Zip offers point-of-sale credit and digital payment services, connecting millions of customers with its global network of tens of thousands of merchants.

We’re proud to be a values-led business and our values - Customer First, Own it, Stronger Together and Change the Game - guide us in everything we do.

In this role, you'll help create an exceptional onboarding experience, deliver impactful learning programs, build trusted relationships across the business, and continuously improve how we enable our Go-to-Market teams. Your work will directly contribute to faster ramp times, stronger adoption of key initiatives, and continuous development of higher-performing teams.

Comfortable leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to drive efficiency, improve workflows, and stay ahead of industry trends.

Experience with an LMS (WorkRamp is a plus).
Experience building out enablement programs.
Familiarity with tools such as Gong, Salesforce, Notion, Google Workspace, or similar GTM technologies.

What We Offer You

The opportunity to shape how our Go-to-Market teams learn, ramp, and perform, to support BlueJ as we scale.
A mission-driven culture where your work directly advances clarity, efficiency, and accessibility in tax research.
Competitive base salary, stock options, and benefits designed to support you and your family.
A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive team that values innovation, respect, and fun.
The excitement of a fast-growing, well-funded company with clear momentum, and the resources to back bold initiatives.

The Core Values that Define Our Culture

We are customer-focused
We put team over self
We are pleasant and playful
We are open to better ideas
We move fast and fix things

What To Expect In The Interview Process

We anticipate a high volume of applicants for this role and are excited to grow our team. A human will review each application and get back to you as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you!

Interview Process

Step 1: Chat with Bailey, our Talent Acquisition Manager
Step 2: Meet with Jamie, Manager of GTM Enablement
Step 3: Present your case study to Jamie, Manager of GTM Enablement, Alex, Business Development Manager, and an additional stakeholder based on availability
Step 4: Wrap up with Ben, our CEO

AI does not make hiring decisions.

Every application is reviewed by a member of our Talent team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans.

We use these tools to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment and we’re committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager - Water Conveyance
new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're driven by a shared purpose—to deliver innovative, technically excellent water infrastructure solutions that strengthen our communities. As a Water Conveyance Project Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to lead complex and meaningful conveyance projects, shape long-term client relationships, and influence the growth of our regional water practice. This role offers the autonomy to lead, the support to succeed, and the career runway to make a lasting impact.

As a Water Conveyance Project Manager, you’ll be charged with leading a team of highly qualified and motivated engineers through the design process, interacting directly with clients to develop and deliver technical conveyance solutions, and mentoring ambitious mid-level engineers. We’ll ask you to grow your career by acting as a highly competent seller-doer that will be empowered to develop and manage projects in a trusting and supported environment.

You’ll serve as a Project Manager/Design Manager leading a technical team, performing technical tasks, and coordinating the use of resources to accomplish multiple, concurrent water infrastructure projects. Your responsibilities may include planning and design related management and technical support roles for various types of conveyance systems such as open channel flow and low-pressure conduit, flow control structures, and pump stations and force mains. Additional assignments may include other water-related civil infrastructure evaluations. You’ll have the opportunity to grow professionally through participation on project teams delivering challenging projects while serving and developing clients.

You’ll be asked to support business development activities in order to grow the local conveyance group. You’ll work with key clients resulting in acquisition of new projects as well as perform the role of Project Manager supporting various projects and programs within a defined client portfolio. You’ll effectively lead and manage project teams throughout all phases of project planning, execution, and closeout; consistent with established project delivery processes to meet the scope, schedule, budget, and other specified requirements stated in each contract.

Using your conveyance technical expertise, you’ll play an integral role in leading and mentoring staff, forming long-term relationships with clients and pursuing new work, building water client portfolios, including strategy development, positioning, proposing, and negotiating contracts. You’ll help others discover what drives them, nurturing their purpose and guiding them forward. Your role will keep our company connected, and we’ll support you with what you need to be successful. But you’re not just a leader – you’re an achiever.  

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's Degree in Civil, Mechanical, and/or Environmental Engineering.
Registration as a Professional Engineer (PE) is required or ability to obtain.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive civil engineering experience.
Demonstrated ability to manage scope, budget, schedule, and technical quality across complex infrastructure projects.

Ideally, you’ll also have

A Master's degree in Civil Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Experience serving various clients involving a wide variety of fields including conveyance pipeline design, project management, water/wastewater pump station design.
Demonstrated ability to lead the design and preparation of plans, specifications, estimates, studies, proposals and/or reports.
Experience with Design-Build and/or EPC projects.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $145,000.00 to $195,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on August 25, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

new_jobs.title: Sales Development Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Description

AEM (Advanced Environmental Monitoring) is the global leader in innovative mission critical weather, wildfire and water monitoring and intelligence solutions. We aim to be the world’s essential source for environmental insights – enabling decisive action and positive outcomes for our customers and their constituents. Our family of innovators offers world-class hydrometeorological technologies and services, including sensors, dataloggers, telemetry, and advanced analytics and software. Our technology and services empower the communities and organizations to survive – and thrive – in the face of escalating environmental risks.

We're hiring a Sales Development Program Manager to own AEM's outbound prospecting function end to end. This is the singular headcount responsible for top-of-funnel pipeline across our commercial verticals, and the person in this seat will build the system, run it, and continuously improve it.

This is a player-coach role. You will run outbound sequences yourself, set sales calls, and optimize what's working, while also building the Apollo automation, AI tooling, and process infrastructure that allows the function to scale. We're looking for someone who already uses AI as a core part of their daily prospecting workflow, not someone who plans to learn it.

Job Responsibilities

Outbound pipeline and prospecting

Own and hit a monthly quota of outbound attended meetings and qualified opportunities across AEM's priority verticals.
Run multi-channel outbound cadences across email, phone, and LinkedIn, working named target accounts with 3-5 contacts per account before moving on.
Identify the right contacts at the right accounts using intent signals, website visitor data, job posting triggers, and seasonal market timing.
Follow up on inbound leads with urgency, enroll them into the right sequences, and hand off qualified meetings to the sales team with clean context.

Apollo automation and AI-assisted prospecting

Own the Apollo instance as AEM's primary outbound operating system, including the sequence library, list hygiene, sending infrastructure, and performance reporting.
Build and continuously optimize AI-assisted prospecting workflows using tools like Claude and ChatGPT to produce sequence copy, call scripts, and account research at scale.
Convert manual sequence steps to automated where quality allows, and maintain clean domain health and list quality to protect sender reputation.
Run a structured weekly review of sequence performance: reply rates, bounce rates, subject line tests, and contact enrollment, and act on what the data says.

ABM and market development

Build and manage intent-based target account lists tied to seasonal events, weather triggers, geography, and ICP fit, and keep them fresh.
Coordinate with marketing on campaign-aligned outbound plays, webinar follow-up, and content-driven sequences.
Bring new top-of-funnel ideas: new verticals, new triggers, new channels. This function is being built from scratch and you have the latitude to shape it.

This job description may not be inclusive of all assigned duties, responsibilities, or aspects of the job described, and may be amended at any time at the sole discretion of the Employer.

Requirements

3 to 5 years of SDR, BDR, or outbound sales experience in a B2B environment with a track record of consistently hitting meeting and pipeline goals.
Hands-on sequencing platform experience in Apollo or an equivalent tool: you have built sequences, managed lists, and read performance data, not just enrolled contacts in someone else's cadence.
Multi-channel cadence execution in practice: email, phone, and LinkedIn working together, with LinkedIn and calling as real parts of the motion, not afterthoughts.
Working experience using AI writing and research tools as part of a daily prospecting workflow: Claude, ChatGPT, or similar. This is a hard requirement, not a nice to have.
Comfortable reading sequence and campaign performance data and making decisions from it. You know the difference between an activity problem and a conversion problem.
Clear, direct written communication. Your cold emails sound like a person, not a template. You can write something under 50 words that actually gets a reply.
Experience or genuine interest in environmental technology, weather monitoring, energy, government, or industrial markets is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Additional Information

This is a remote opportunity that can be done from anywhere in the continental United States and/or Canada
Must be eligible to work in the U.S. or Canada without company sponsorship, now or in the future, for employment-based work authorization. F-1 visa holders with Optional Practical Training (OPT) who will require H-1B status, TNs, or current H-1B visa holders will not be considered. H1-B and green card sponsorship is not available for this position.

US Benefits include: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short-Term & Long-Term Disability & 401k match of up to 3%.

Location

Job
Type

Role Overview:

We are hiring for one of our clients, seeking a Strategic Project Lead, MD/Medical Expertise to work on a full-time basis. This role requires a medical doctorate or equivalent expertise to lead cross-functional projects in healthcare technology. You will collaborate with senior stakeholders to align project objectives with business and clinical goals.

Key Responsibilities:

• Develop and execute strategic project plans for medical technology initiatives with measurable outcomes.
• Lead cross-functional teams including product, engineering, and clinical experts to deliver solutions.
• Identify and mitigate risks related to project timelines, budgets, and regulatory compliance.
• Coordinate with medical teams to ensure projects meet clinical requirements and standards.
• Monitor project progress using data-driven metrics and adjust strategies as needed to achieve targets.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

• Must hold an MD or equivalent medical degree with 5+ years of clinical or medical technology experience.
• Proven track record leading strategic projects in healthcare, biotechnology, or related fields.
• Strong understanding of medical regulations, compliance, and ethical considerations.
• Ability to translate complex medical concepts into business requirements for technical teams.

Program Manager, Risk Operations GTM Enablement
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Risk PMO team protects Stripe’s revenue and drives cross-functional strategy for company-level and org-level priorities. As Stripe operates across an increasingly complex and fast-moving global regulatory environment, one of our most important functions is ensuring that our largest, most strategic users can grow with us—compliantly, confidently, and at speed.

We sit at the intersection of Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and GTM—serving as the bridge between teams coordinating massive programs with global, wide-reaching impact. We build durable systems that enable strong collaboration across functions and seamless experiences for our users.

If you're energized by high-stakes, ambiguous problems and thrive on building programs from scratch in environments where the rules are still being written—we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

You will define, own, and execute program strategies for large-scale regulatory initiatives, operating with significant autonomy across a portfolio of global projects.

This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor (IC) role. While you will influence senior leadership and set strategic direction, you are also the primary driver of execution. You will need to zoom out to design the long-term vision, and zoom in to manage the details—building templates, tracking deliverables, writing documentation, and directly unblocking cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

Own and execute high-stakes global programs end-to-end, from initial strategy and scoping to project planning, day-to-day tracking, and change management
Drive step-change improvements in our operational processes, rolling up your sleeves to build systems and workflows that directly improve business outcomes and top-line metrics
Bridge compliance and commercial strategy by partnering with GTM and account leadership to turn complex regulatory requirements into a competitive advantage that builds deep user trust
Build and run operating models across diverse cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance), keeping highly distributed workstreams aligned and accountable
Serve as a trusted advisor by preparing strategic reviews for senior stakeholders and managing critical escalations
Translate user friction into program evolution by establishing structured, data-driven approaches to gather user feedback and turning those insights into actionable product and operational improvements
Diagnose and resolve systemic operational gaps before they impact our users, building self-healing processes and scalable internal infrastructure
Champion Stripe’s Operating Principles by fostering a high-performance culture that values rigorous thinking, rapid execution, and putting users first

Who you are

You are a highly strategic operator, a masterful communicator, and a systems thinker with operational grit. You thrive in the gray area, possessing the ability to translate ambiguous global challenges into elegant, structured, and highly actionable operational frameworks.

You are a natural leader who leads by influence and by example. You have a deep empathy for the user, an unyielding bias toward action, and you take pride in the craft of execution. No problem is too complex for you to deconstruct, and no detail is too small if it impacts the user experience.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of experience in Program Management, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, or Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
Hands-on execution track record: Proven ability to work independently as an individual contributor, managing complex, multi-stakeholder project plans and deliverables from inception to completion
Exceptional communication & storytelling: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to distill highly complex, technical, or regulatory topics into clear, succinct, and persuasive narratives to external and senior audiences
Systems and infrastructure builder: Deep experience designing, launching, and scaling complex cross-functional operating models, feedback loops, and PMO frameworks
Growth mindset: A high willingness to learn, adapt quickly to changing environments, and actively seek and act on feedback to continuously improve

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in high-growth technology or fintech environments
Deep cross-functional partnership: Prior experience working alongside Engineering, Product, Legal, Compliance, and GTM/Sales
Data fluency: Experience leveraging data visualization tools and analytical frameworks to back up strategic decisions and measure program success

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Federal Realty Investment Trust is a proven leader in the ownership, operation, development and redevelopment of premium retail real estate in the country's best markets. While Federal Realty is one of the largest publicly traded real estate investment trusts in the country, as measured by the value of our assets, we're functionally a small company by most standards and we operate that way. Team members with initiative and proven ability get involved in many facets of executing Federal’s business plan. We encourage you to look us up on LinkedIn and follow Federal Realty Investment Trust.

We are currently seeking a Project Manager, Construction and Tenant Services to join our West Coast Tenant Coordination team. The Project Manager is responsible for the management and coordination of projects within their assigned portfolio of properties. Project responsibilities are of a varying and complex nature including, but not limited to, coordinating landlord and tenant work related tasks, status reporting, budgeting, estimating, scheduling and coordinating any tasks required to deliver possession to a new tenant. The Project Manager is the liaison between Federal Realty, the tenant, and the tenant’s architects, consultants, and contractors throughout the planning and construction process of the assigned project. The position will be based in either our El Segundo, CA or La Mesa, CA office.

Responsibilities

Responsible for “driving” the landlord and tenant design, permitting and construction process to ensure achievement of “best possible” rent commencement dates for all projects as assigned
Proactively performs all tasks related to gathering information required by leasing to market tenant spaces
Manages and coordinates construction projects from conceptual estimating through project close out on new and existing retail project buildings throughout a specified region
Ensures coordination of all assigned projects with appropriate Federal Realty departments, consultants, tenants, and 3rd party managers
Creates and coordinates conceptual estimates under the direction of Director Construction & Tenant Services for lease budgetary purposes
Drafts and reviews construction exhibits upon request by Leasing or Legal
Reviews leases for milestone dates, potential penalties, and other information related to the project
Reviews and approves Landlord and Tenant construction drawings to ensure compliance with lease, budget, schedule and design requirements
Reviews certificates of insurance
Responsible for the regular reporting of status for all work in process in Salesforce
Responsible for contracting, oversight, managing budget and timely delivery of all new lease required Landlord’s work
Coordinates directly with Legal, Leasing, Asset Management and Development to ensure that lease language and terms of delivery are reasonable and achievable.
Troubleshoots design and construction issues as they arise
Provides scheduling and planning information to appropriate internal departments, as required

Qualifications

3-7 years of tenant coordination and/or project/construction management experience
Experience with design and construction of retail properties
Experience with design and construction coordination and project management
Degree in Architecture, Construction Management or a related management degree, preferred
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present information effectively
Excellent organizational and analytical skills to include multi-tasking and the ability to successfully manage a large volume of projects
Demonstrated customer service orientation and proven ability to work, manage, and gain consensus with multiple stakeholders
Proven ability to provide efficient, timely, reliable and courteous service to customers
Demonstrated ability to comprehend, analyze, and interpret complex documents and solve problems involving several options in situations, requires advanced analytical and quantitative skills
Experience in reading and understanding architectural drawings
Proven ability to perform financial analysis/reporting of construction cost
Excellent negotiation skills
Solid computer skills (MS Office) required
Graphics skills are a plus
Ability to travel to project sites as needed in California

Salary Range: The typical total compensation range for this role is $125,000–$170,000 per year, inclusive of base salary and any applicable bonus. To ensure a fair and competitive offer, we take into account your job-related skills, experience, relevant trainings, and certifications.
